items.text: Captains, a Skull and Bones maintenance is underway 🛠️
[p align="start"] 📅 Thursday 27th August
[p align="start"]⏰ 8AM CEST / 4PM AET / 11PM PT (26th AUG)
[p align="start"]⏳ ~2 hours
[p align="start"]Item Salvage
Shifted the Salvage option after selecting an item to the second action in the list.
[p align="start"] Stability
Fixed an issue where players could not progress past the splash screen on devices with lower hardware specifications.
Improved client stability
[p align="start"]Contracts
“The Unbending Flame” - Fixed an issue where the interaction prompt at the hideout missing if “Flicker of Destiny” had not been previously completed.
“A Trail Renewed” - Fixed an issue where the outpost NPC was missing on Low settings.
“Treacherous Trail” – Fixed an issue where the cutscene camera was sometimes unintentionally excessively zoomed in
“Junk-to-Junk” – Fixed an issue where cargo would appear vanished when players are sunk during the first step of the contract

[p align="start"] Dev Note: Our investigation findings for the Junk-to-Junk contract issue show that the cargo does not actually vanish, but the player’s ship is switched to a different ship than the previously selected ship. Switching to the previously selected ship will allow players to recover their “lost” cargo.
[p align="start"]Activities & World Events
Fixed an issue where all ships from the event area despawn abruptly when the Abyssal Herald elite warship is sunk in the 3rd wave of the Heralds of the Abyss world event.
[p align="start"]Boosts
Fixed an issue where activating multiple Teuling Favour boosts concurrently would result in a “Rotative store failure” error.
[p align="start"]Camera
Fixed an issue where the camera would be stuck in an incorrect orientation when switching World Tiers while in a dialogue or cutscene
[p align="start"]Faction War
Fixed an issue where the War Assets reward track was awarding lower quantities of items than intended.
[p align="start"]UI
Fixed an issue where placeholder text was seen on the character creation screen
Fixed an issue with visual artifacts in the main menu screen
Fixed an issue where the premium edition pop-up would unintentionally re-appear on the main menu when entering the game for the first time each season
[p align="start"]

And with it, the skies bleed crimson, reflected on waters as of yet undisturbed.

Are you ready, Captain?

Perk: Infernal Embers
Weapon hits on target enemies apply one stack of Ember, up to 20 stacks for 5 seconds, which decays one by one.
Ember decreases Armor Rating by 2% and Fire Resistance by 2% per stack.
Gain a stack of Inferno when hitting an enemy with max Ember stacks, up to 10 stacks, which lasts 5 seconds.
Inferno decreases Reload Time by 0.5% and increases Weapon Damage by 3% per stack.
Allied XSML, SML and MED ships within 500 meters gains half of the bonus provided by Inferno.
Upgraded Perk: Infernal Skies
On attaining max stacks of Inferno, the next weapon hit on an enemy target will trigger a fiery explosion dealing 200% of your Weapon Damage as Fire damage. The effect has a 20 second cooldown.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/be1138fbcb69abff8156b24f2207f48890395f84.jpg"]
A new enemy faction, The Abyssal Fleet, has invaded the Indian Ocean. It can be encountered predominantly on World Tier 4.
Featuring challenging enemies equipped with Armored Weakpoints, the Fleet is made all the more deadlier with proficiency in impacting your ship's ability to repair in combat.
Be prepared, Captain. These challenging fights will take time and require you to pay attention to incoming reinforcements – lest you be overwhelmed and quickly outnumbered.
Heralds of the Abyss World Event
A new World Event is available in World Tier 4. It can be started from its buoy on the map.
Trigger this event at your own risk and defend yourself against waves of invading Abyssal Fleet ships.

Those waves will culminate in a showdown against the new Abyssal Herald elite warship. Capable of a wide range of attacks, you must be vigilant and respond to them quickly to stay alive. Captains with a keen aim will be able to target vital weakpoints to assist them in taking down this new threat.
[p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/151ad909b00d1e2f9dbf3758ff5a3dd842a1c1d4.jpg"]

Abyssal Essence can be obtained from the Abyssal Fleet and can be used in mod transfers or at Blackwood for additional rewards, such as cosmetics, Adept Modded Weapons, and the craneless Barque skin: Crown of Ruin.

Alongside this, defeating Heralds of the Abyss provides a chance to obtain Adept Modded Weapons and Mythic Exclusive Mods. These particular mods are not obtainable from the Blacksmith via the regular methods.
This season’s available weapon categories of Mythic Exclusive Mods are: Culverins, Demicannons, Long Guns and Ballistas. Additional weapon types will be added in the future.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/cc3180278db9530c0fc77379ede838e48b436a41.jpg"]
A new service is available at the Blacksmith: Modification Transfer.

This feature allows for the transfer of Modifications between different equipment of the same kind. Singular or multiple Modifications can be transferred from a Source item to a Target item provided there is a valid slot unlocked.
Once the modifications have been transferred, the source weapon will be destroyed in the process.
Transferring Modifications will require a new material, Ascension Flux. This material can be obtained from salvaging Ascended items.
Seasonal Mastery Loadouts are now available, enabling players to save multiple Mastery Node and Perk allocations to switch between them seamlessly.
Mastery Loadouts can be set or changed in the Ship Loadout menu for ease of use when changing ships.
[p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/b85e6e34f011506069b6098ab31d05835ebdeb0a.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/275fcd5469a57d04de770e6424b2f0befac6857b.jpg"]
[p align="center"]
Players can now save up to 10 Mastery Skill Tree Loadouts.
Loadouts can be edited and saved directly from the Mastery Tree UI.
Mastery Loadouts can be saved per ship, allowing players to swap ships without having to manually rebuild their tree each time.
A new Ship Details screen has been added giving players a complete overview of their ship's stats, consolidating all sources in one place: Ship, Weapons & Armor, Furniture, and Mastery Tree.
This screen is accessible from both Ship Loadout and My Fleet.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/0254590b81b547de41542a2f7e5ce42ef25d244c.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/03cde11a488fadd55944ffce33129346e03dcadc.jpg"]

Further improvements to sorting and filtering across menus will be available:
A Sort Order button has been added, allowing players to easily switch between Ascending and Descending order in the item list.
Filter options are now grouped into clear categories for easier browsing.
A Reset Filter button has been added to quickly clear all selected filters at once.
The tick/untick icons have been updated to better reflect a "Multiple Choice" selection style.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/cfc3040167793c6a595efb87462819860882be7a.jpg"]
The Sort & Filter panel for the Warehouse Inventory has been moved to the left side of the screen, so it no longer overlaps and obscures the item list behind it.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/91eb39fd4c8909dcd469375f255d718fe5c21471.jpg"]

Addition of Fleet Categories for better navigation.
Daily logins will now be available for the whole season.
Blackwood stocks have been updated to include Y3S1 equipment from Faction War and Smuggler Pass.
Galleon blueprint can now be purchased from Blackwood.
Blackwood now has an Abyss tab to purchase new Adept Mod weapons.
Time Limited Event vendors (Halloween and Darktide Lullaby) now also include new Adept weapons with Ascended Weapon Chest.
Added the ability to manually trigger the Ship Aura effects via the Action Wheel
Year 3 Season 2 introduces a refreshed Seasonal Mastery Tree, featuring new Seasonal Perks, Major Skills and minor adjustments in the skill tree layout.
This seasons’ Perks revolve around a new mechanic called “Impetus”
Impetus is a combat resource that is acquired through utilizing the new Seasonal Perks and is likewise consumed to gain buffs and trigger powerful effects in other Seasonal Perks.

\[Level 10 Perk] Relentless Force: Generate 1 stack of Impetus (max 10) for every 8 weapon hits on enemies. Demicannons require 4 times as many hits. Generating Impetus increases Weapon Damage and Repair Amount by 15% for 5 seconds.
\[Level 30 Perk] Weakness Finder: Generating Impetus adds a 20% chance to convert any weapon shot into a weakpoint hit for 5 seconds.
\[Level 50 Perk] Firepower Order: When at 10 stacks of Impetus, fire an Auxiliary Weapon to consume 10 stacks and convert all weapon hits to weakpoint hits for 8 seconds.
The Mastery level requirement for the Tier 3 Seasonal Perk has been reduced to level 50 (previously level 60).

Although the raw Infamy requirements per level have been increased, this is balanced alongside a larger adjustment in Infamy gain across the World Tiers (see section “World Tier Infamy Rebalance” below). Overall, this adjustment achieves a steadier levelling pace at the early Mastery Levels, while also reducing the steep climb in infamy requirements at the later levels.

Returning players from previous seasons will earn a head start on Mastery Points at the beginning of a new season, based on their final progress in the prior season, accelerating their journey toward Mastery 80:
Previously Level 60 > Start at Level 5 next season
Previously Level 70 > Start at Level 10 next season
Previously Level 80 > Start at Level 15 next season
With the introduction of a new Season, Seasonal Affixes have been refreshed, introducing 4 new Affixes and 1 returning Affix.
Seasonal Journey
A new Seasonal Journey is available and will cover new content such as the Junk Ship Trial and this season’s quests.
New to this Season will be additional Mastery Point rewards on the Journey. Coupled with Mastery Levels, Captains can reach a total of 90 Mastery Points to use.
Demi-Cannons
Increased weapon damage when fired within 100m range.
Weapon damage falloff now starts at 120m and beyond.

🛠 Dev Note: This is part 1 of an effort to align Demi-Cannons closer to shotguns. Part 2 will look at reload time and damage adjustments, with the long-term goal of enabling distinct Demi-Cannon variations, not just perk-wise, but also in handling, range, etc.
Agni's Fury
Fixed Agni's Fury to use actual projectiles for hit detection (previously used ray cast, causing visible desync on hits).
Magazine size increased from 30 → 90.
Damage per shot reduced from 619 → 206.
Reload time reduced from 1s → 0.333s.
🛠 Dev Note: An overall balance pass following the hit detection fix, adjusting magazine size, damage per shot, and reload time accordingly.
Furniture
Caustic Spall Station (Minor/Epic)
Projectile speed bonus scaling cap for Flooding damage reduced from 30% → 15%. All other effects are unchanged.
🛠 Dev Note: Caustic Spall Station is overperforming. The bonus cap has been nerfed from 30% to 15%.
Gimbal Ring Stores (Major/Epic)
Replaced "Hitting a target over 180m away increases Demi Cannon damage by 17% for 12s" with: For every Demi-Cannon weapon equipped, increase weapon damage of equipped weapons by 5%.
Projectile speed and Maximum Range bonuses for Demi-Cannon weapons unchanged.
🛠 Dev Note: Adjusted to align with the Demi-Cannons’ adjustment.
Ship Perks
Frigate – Grit
Armor gained per Grit stack increased from 40 → 50 (up to 10 stacks).

🛠 Dev Note: The Frigate currently lacks offensive modifiers but has the highest Hull health and Brace strength among all ships. This change further improves durability and allows more flexibility to invest Seasonal Mastery points into offensive nodes.
Frigate – Resolve
Brace Strength restored on activation increased from 10% → 20%.
Schooner – Fury
Chance to trigger Fury on self increased from 20% → 30%.
Broadside Weapon Damage boost while Fury is active increased from 20% → 30%.
🛠 Dev Note: Fury's proc-based design felt like it needed a buff to land with more impact.

The Job Board has been overhauled in Y3S2.

Seasonal Job Board contracts are no longer tracked through the Journal. Instead, The Job Board now runs on a dedicated cycle of daily and weekly Smuggler Pass challenges, giving you a steady stream of objectives to chase and rewards such as Smuggler Points, Guildmarks and Deep Iron throughout the season.
To get started, an Infamy quest “Hired Help” will be available at the start of the season in the Journal. This quest will direct you to the Job Board in Sainte-Anne and Telok Penjarah.
Contract Tiers & Rewards
Contracts come in three tiers of difficulty, each carrying their own share of Smuggler Points and Guildmarks:
Easy : 150 Smuggler Points
Medium : 300 Smuggler Points & 100 Guildmarks
Hard : 1200 to 2000 Smuggler Points
The challenge pool is designed to encourage you to engage with the full breadth of the Indian Ocean's dangers.
Moonshine & Honorless
Challenges tied to Moonshine and Honorless events will also be accessible directly through the Job Board this season.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/b4f234ff505ade78164856293039aff9bf9376f1.jpg"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/e94428a09b743dc87b4ebee93202c877683f35c1.jpg"]

The Milestone Rewards also feature a Ship Upgrade Material Bundle, which has materials specifically suited for upgrading the Junk at 6/7. Other Bundles for alternative Upgrade Levels are offered throughout the Smuggler Pass tracks.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/e2e214d81e0e0f1fa2f4c92daa5e0c0ee0507f7b.jpg"]

A new Armor, Pyroclasm, is available in the Quartermaster track along with Junk Upgrade Bundle which offers resources to upgrade Junk to level 2.

New Quests: Freeman's Trail Continues

Lucian Harrow isn't the only one closing in on Uricko Freeman's secrets - and this season, the race gets personal. Team up with a survivor from Freeman's own crew as old rumors resurface, and a dangerous rival fleet moves to claim what's buried at Bukit Candi first.
A Trail Renewed: Pick up where last season left off as a new lead reopens the hunt for Freeman's legacy.
The True Cargo : Not everything Harrow's crew is hauling is what it seems. Some secrets are worth fighting for.
The Unbending Flame : The trail comes to a head. What you walk away with may matter more than the treasure itself.
Expect political maneuvering, a few surprises about who you can actually trust, and a season that leaves you holding onto something far more valuable than gold.
Junk to Junk : Ever wanted to captain a Junk? A new side objective puts you at the helm of one for a hands-on sea trial - handle her, prove her worth, and bring her home in one piece.

releases.displayName: Year 3 Season 2 Development Update: IPP17 Recap & Community Q&A

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/e5887984cb6ba087033508f962d63c3fccaf17e5.jpg"]Hi Captains,

[p align="start"]We've just wrapped up Insider Program Phase 17, where we tested some of the features coming in Year 3 Season 2, and we sat down (well, went live) to share where the team is today, talk through what we've learned from recent feedback, and answer your questions live.

[p align="start"]As we said at the start of Year 3, we're committed to shaping the Year 3 Roadmap alongside the community, and this stream was another opportunity to keep you updated on that journey. Our Lead Game Designer Samuel Quek joined to cover everything from the new enemy to Combat 2.0, mod transfer and a few things we hadn't planned to tease.
[p align="start"]For the full stream VOD, click here. Below, we've pulled together the key moments and answers that give a broader picture of where development progress is heading.
[p align="start"]Q: IPP17 has just wrapped up. How did it go? What features were tested, and where does the team stand on development progress heading into Year 3 Season 2?

[p align="start"]A: Overall, IPP17 gave us exactly what we needed: real hands-on feedback on content before they're finalized so we can address and iterate on it before the season launch. The Insider Program is one of the most valuable tools in our process precisely because players test features in their raw, unpolished state and still take the time to give us detailed, constructive feedback. That matters a lot to us.
[p align="start"]This phase covered the new Abyssal enemy faction and its world event, the Junk, ammunition removal, Mod Transfer, Seasonal Mastery loadout, QoL improvements, and more.
[p align="start"]Here's a high-level picture of what we heard and how we responded:
[p align="start"]New enemy faction (Abyssal): Insiders flagged difficulty spikes, reward clarity, and some confusion between the fleet and the event itself.

[p align="start"]We've rebalanced some smaller enemies and will keep on iterating difficulty balancing as the season progresses. We have also finished implementing the boss encounter that was missing from the IPP build and improved the overall VFX and atmosphere of the event.
[p align="start"]The Junk: With overall positive feedback, some highlighted issues with aiming, with the junk’s perks not standing out strongly enough.

[p align="start"]After digging into the data, we identified specific issues with aiming angles and camera behaviour tied to the ship's unique shape. Those have been addressed. Junk perk has been slightly buffed after the IP. More on Junk’s playstyle and role in combat is coming at the August 12th stream.

[p align="start"]Ammunition removal: Some insiders supported the removal, with some asking for alternative systems and compensation. Removal remains targeted for one of the later post-launch updates, giving us the time to do it cleanly and compensate players properly - part of a broader effort to reduce friction across the game's economy.

[p align="start"]Item Ascension & Mod Transfer: The main feedback was that Mod Transfer felt too restrictive. For Y3S2, transfers are now possible across all items within the same equipment category - a significant expansion. We'll continue monitoring the system post-launch before going further.
[p align="start"]Seasonal Mastery: Players welcomed the loadout system but raised concerns about resets, carry-over, and pacing past level 50.

We’ve implemented the suggestion of increasing Mastery Loadout slots to 10; we understand that resetting progress can feel frustrating. We’re reviewing carry-over values for future seasons, and the progression pace has been adjusted past level 50 to make it significantly smoother and adjusted Infamy gains at higher Ship Ratings. We’ll make further adjustments to both progression pace and difficulty balancing based on community feedback. Long term, as a further improvement to the Mastery Loadout, we’re considering the possibility of expanding on the switch ship feature so that any type of loadout could be switched from this menu.

[p align="start"]*Besides working towards the Y3S2 launch, while it's still early days, the team has also begun drafting the Year 4 roadmap. The same commitment to naval combat as the core experience continues, and Year 4 will be built on the depth we're establishing throughout Year 3. Expect more focus on activities that test different skills, ways for players to compare and showcase their mastery, and stronger tools for group play. Details will follow as we get closer.
[p align="start"]Q: Will we get more weapon types for every deck, beyond Demicannons and Culverins?

[p align="start"]A: Expanding loadout diversity is one of the core goals of Combat 2.0. We want weapons to offer meaningful, distinct strategic choices, not just numerical variations. We're not in a position to confirm specific new weapon types today, but this is a priority direction.
[p align="start"]Q: Could we get a Xebec?

[p align="start"]A: It's one of the options we're actively narrowing down for Year 4. The ship roadmap for Year 3 is locked and already in production, but Year 4 is still being shaped, and community input on what ships you want to see is very welcome right now.
[p align="start"]Q: What can you share about the Season 4 ship?

[p align="start"]A: Production has started. It will be a large ship, but its playstyle and potential equipment loadout is something that's never been seen before in the game. More details coming soon.
[p align="start"]Q: Any chance of XL ships?

[p align="start"]A: The challenge with XL ships is that the existing world wasn't designed with them in mind, you can squeeze a Galleon into a river, but a true XL ship simply wouldn't fit. We're looking at whether they could work as situational use ships with specific deployment contexts, and whether players would be okay with that kind of limitation. Nothing to confirm yet, but we're not writing it off.
[p align="start"]Q: Could we see a rework or buff to the Frigate?

[p align="start"]A: We're hearing you on ship balance. Combat 2.0 , which is actively in development , is specifically designed to ensure the competitiveness and viability of all ships and equipment across every class. We don't have a standalone Frigate rework to announce right now, but this is exactly the kind of feedback that's shaping that work.
[p align="start"]Q: Is the introduction of ships of the line as enemies possible in the short or medium term?
[p align="start"]A: Short and medium term , probably not. Long term ,yes, we've started discussions and it's on the table.
[p align="start"]Q: Are we going to get the Man o' War from AC Black Flag Resynced?
[p align="start"]A: Can't confirm or deny at this stage, but it is technically feasible for us to bring in ships that appear in other games such as Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced. 😉
[p align="start"]Q: More updates on PvP improvements ,PvP world tier, Combat 2.0, new PvP events. Any timelines?

[p align="start"]A: We hear you, and we know you've been waiting. Combat 2.0 is actively in development , it will enable wider loadout and gameplay diversity, improve the clarity of combat stats and perks, and ensure all ships and equipment are competitive and viable. No release date to share just yet, but this is real, ongoing work. On PvP-specific improvements like world tier integration and new events , we'll share more as soon as we have concrete updates to give you. Combat 2.0 is the foundation everything else follows from.
[p align="start"]Q: Will 6v6 ever return to Death Tides?
[p align="start"]A: Not a priority at this stage. If we see significant demand, we'll reconsider.
[p align="start"]Q: Will more Ultimates be added to Death Tides?
[p align="start"]A: No plans at the moment.
[p align="start"]Q: What about the Death Tides Pass overall?

[p align="start"]A: We want to take a broader look at the entire Death Tides experience rather than making isolated improvements to individual pieces. That holistic review is coming ,but it ties into Combat 2.0 first. Once combat balance is in better shape, the mode can evolve properly.
[p align="start"]Q: Can you look at the damage output of small NPC sharpshooter/skirmisher ships in WT4? They can almost destroy you in one volley.

[p align="start"]A: We've heard this consistently and we've acted on it. WT4 difficulty has been rebalanced in Y3S2 to bring enemy threat levels closer together , SR33+ spawn damage scaling and health are specifically being adjusted. We've also nerfed the Caustic Spall Station: its bonus cap is being reduced from 30% to 15%, which directly addresses the extreme damage spikes that Seasonal Mastery can amplify. Looking further ahead, Combat 2.0 will take on the broader balance extremes more comprehensively.
[p align="start"]Q: Won't more World Tiers split the playerbase?

[p align="start"]A: Based on our current player numbers, adding new World Tiers won't reduce average server population. When players feel a server is empty, it's most often because that server has been running for a while ,we have a time limit after which new players stop being matchmade into it for technical reliability. New tiers won't change the per-server player count.
[p align="start"]Q: Is a rework of the seasonal system planned ,restructuring duration, content delivery, and so on?

[p align="start"]A: While we are not planning to change the duration of our seasons at the moment, we are looking at how we release content throughout the seasons. Some of the content we have planned for Y3S2 will be coming in later in the season for example. If you have any feedback or suggestions on the duration or the way we deliver content in a season, we’d love to read about it.
[p align="start"]Q: What about old bounties and contracts like Fangs of the Fara that are currently unreceivable?

[p align="start"]A: We're doing a full revision of bounties and contracts. Some have been temporarily taken out because they're being overhauled ,when that work is done, they'll come back, either in their reworked form or as new versions.
[p align="start"]Q: Will there be a rework or better rewards for Strongholds and Forts?

[p align="start"]A: We made improvements to Stronghold rewards in Y3S1 to better align effort with reward, especially at higher World Tiers. That said, this is something we review every season. We've heard the feedback about running out of ascension parts and upgrade materials ,those are the kinds of specific gaps we look to address. At the same time, we do try to keep different content responsible for different types of rewards so that activities don't all feel identical. It won't end here.
[p align="start"]Q: Will there be a major fort for WT3 and WT4?
[p align="start"]A: No plans for new major forts right now. However, a brand new World Event is planned for World Tier 4 in Y3S2.
[p align="start"]Q: Is there a rework of Helm Contracts planned? They feel obsolete.
[p align="start"]A: Yes, Helm Contracts will be reworked.
[p align="start"]Q: Are you planning to expand the game's lore significantly?

[p align="start"]A: The game lore is expanding with every season. We are also working on streamlining the current lore and how players experience it from the very beginning of the game all the way to our end game.

[p align="start"]Beyond that we also want to put some efforts into improving our Codex, to ensure every in-game item is listed, every item locations is trackable, descriptions are updated, and introducing a narrative content viewer allowing players to see your full story progression at a glance and track narrative contracts directly from that menu. This is the foundation we're building for deeper, more meaningful lore expansion. We're not in a position to detail specific story destinations just yet, but there's a lot more of this world left to discover.
[p align="start"]Q: Are we going to get new factions ,Hubac Twins, Li Tian Ning? When will the British Navy be in the game?

[p align="start"]A: Another faction is being introduced to Faction War starting with Y3S2. We can't confirm timelines for other factions right now, but we are looking into adding existing factions and completely new ones to the game through Faction War.
[p align="start"]Q: Will the BTA finally get some love?
[p align="start"]A: The BTA is something we're seriously considering as a faction to be introduced through Faction War. But no timeline commitment at this point.
[p align="start"]Q: Could we see BTA and Portugal cosmetic sets for players who've been after them since launch?
[p align="start"]A: That's something we can look into, yes.
[p align="start"]Q: Has the implementation of faction-specific flags been considered?

[p align="start"]A: Yes, and we've looked into it internally. It requires more work than it might seem ,faction flags are tied to our existing emblem system, and we want to make sure players who want them and players who don't can both control how they appear on their ship. It's something we're interested in for the future, nothing to announce yet.
[p align="start"]Q: Will the Royal African Company become part of the story?
[p align="start"]A: No plans for this at the moment.
[p align="start"]Q: Seasonal Mastery ,could we see improvements to health levels in the seasonal tree?

[p align="start"]A: This is something we're always evaluating as part of our ongoing balance efforts. Each season, we review and update the Seasonal Mastery tree, looking at both the types of nodes available and the values of those upgrades

[p align="start"]For Y3S2 specifically, we've also fine-tuned AI balance across all World Tiers, with some of the biggest changes being felt in World Tier 4. Our goal is to improve survivability not just through the Seasonal Tree itself, but by balancing the overall combat experience.

[p align="start"]We'll continue monitoring player feedback and gameplay data after launch, and if further adjustments are needed whether that's to the Seasonal Mastery tree, AI balance, or other progression systems， we'll continue iterating on them.
[p align="start"]Q: Could you make an improvement to the Seasonal Mastery carry-over and pacing?

[p align="start"]A: Yes. For Y3S2, mastery loadout slots are being increased to 10. Carry-over values are being reviewed to reduce reset frustration. And the progression pace past level 50 has been significantly smoothed out. We've also increased Infamy gain from Elite Warships and Sea Monsters at higher Ship Ratings so that the climb to higher mastery levels keeps pace with World Tier progression.
[p align="start"]Q: Are you planning to improve William's shop? Will it ever include Ascended weapon rewards?

[p align="start"]A: Yes ,a brand new Abyssal section is opening in Blackwood's shop in Y3S2, tied to the new seasonal activities and enemies. It will include Ascended weapons as well as some curated weapons. This is the new section equivalent of a dedicated shop for the season's content.
[p align="start"]Q: Will world events and bosses receive significantly better rewards?

[p align="start"]A: We continuously review reward pools and look for specific gaps ,the feedback around items like Deep Iron has been heard, and we're making adjustments to improve access to materials like that. Different activities will always serve different reward purposes, but we want every activity to feel worth the effort.
[p align="start"]Q: Are there any major QoL improvements coming in Y3S2?
[p align="start"]A: Yes , and Y3S2 delivers on several of them directly:
Mastery Loadout slots increased to 10
Carry-over values are being reviewed to reduce reset frustration
Progression pace past level 50 has been significantly smoothed
Gear can now be transferred on newly crafted ships
Infamy gain from Elite Warships and Sea Monsters has been increased at higher SRs
Event and My Fleet menus are getting QoL improvements
[p align="start"]Longer-term, we're exploring expanding the switch-ship menu so any loadout type can be swapped from it.
[p align="start"]Q: Could we get a private testing area to test builds, damage, and healing without interruptions?

[p align="start"]A: It's something we're actively exploring. We understand the value of having a dedicated space where players can freely test builds, compare damage and healing, and experiment with different loadouts without interruptions.

[p align="start"]At the moment, the idea is still in its early stages. We're looking into what form a feature like this could take, where it would fit within the game, and, most importantly, what players would want from a testing area to make it genuinely useful.
[p align="start"]We don't have anything to announce just yet, but it's definitely a topic we're discussing and evaluating.
[p align="start"]Q: What's being done to increase community communications and engagement in-game? Looking for Group improvements? Will chat ever work reliably? In-game direct messaging?

[p align="start"]A: Social features are a top priority for Year 4 ,we're looking at how to extend connection beyond individual servers and improve the tools players have to find and communicate with each other. We'll share more as those plans solidify. Chat reliability is something we continue to work on.
[p align="start"]Q: Has the implementation of new animations for when the Helm is in use been considered?

[p align="start"]A: Yes ,we're currently doing a broader pass on Captain animations, including helm interactions and on-land movement. The work is in progress. We don't have a release timeline, but it will roll out when it's ready.
[p align="start"]Q: Will Armor Transmog ever be implemented?
[p align="start"]A: Yes, it will be implemented ,we're just not sure when yet. It's in the works.
[p align="start"]Q: Will the HUD receive a revamp in the future?
[p align="start"]A: Yes. We're going through a broader review of menus and HUD elements across the game.
[p align="start"]Q: Could we get improvements to the Death Tides Pass or a system like the Smuggler's?

[p align="start"]A: We want to take a broader look at the entire Death Tides experience rather than making isolated fixes. That includes the reward tracks, progression, and overall player experience. This ties into Combat 2.0 ,once the combat foundation is in better shape, Death Tides can evolve properly.
[p align="start"]Q: Can we get an in-game shop where we can pay Silver to get old cosmetics?

[p align="start"]A: We're actively looking at more ways to make older cosmetics available to players. Rather than a single Silver storefront, we're interested in bringing them back through a variety of avenues, gameplay activities, events, and other reward opportunities. We want players to have fun in the process of earning them, not just visit a menu. We're also looking at how we can improve and build on experiences like Glory Adorned events. More to come as those plans take shape.
[p align="start"]Q: Is there going to be Nordic cosmetics?
[p align="start"]A: We're always happy to hear more inspiration requests from the community. This is something we could look into if requests are high.
[p align="start"]Q: Is there any interest in altering how cosmetic auras function?

[p align="start"]A: Yes, and this is coming soon. In an upcoming update, you'll be able to trigger your equipped ship aura on demand via the quick-access wheel, similar to how fireworks work today. More control over when you showcase it.
[p align="start"]Q: Will the cosmetic store receive an update where players can buy more individual parts of a set?

[p align="start"]A: We're interested in exploring this, and want to better understand what players are after. Today, bundles come with discounts over individual items, so it's not a simple change. Let us know which specific items or types you'd most want to buy individually ,that feedback shapes how we approach the store.
[p align="start"]Q: About the AC: Black Flag Resynced Emblem ,any chance of getting more from the Black Flag Resynced collaboration?
[p align="start"]A: Yes. We have more cross-promotional content planned . Stay tuned, details are coming soon.
[p align="start"]Q: Should there be a player competition for designing ship ornaments?

[p align="start"]A: We love this idea and want to build on it. We had our first trial with the Emblem Design Contest, and the response was encouraging. The next step could be a full ship collection or even a Captain outfit competition. The caveat is that the bigger the cosmetic set, the longer the pipeline from competition to in-game, but it's something we genuinely want to do.
[p align="start"]Q: Will there ever be a way to get missed Twitch Drops?

[p align="start"]A: Good news ,a rotation of old Twitch Drops is planned throughout Year 3. If you missed a drop, you'll have another chance. We'll share the schedule when confirmed. And for streams going forward, we're looking at extending the configuration window so more people have a chance to claim.
[p align="start"]Q: Will there be a Year 3 edition of the game?
[p align="start"]A: We're currently working on updating the game's offerings to better reflect Year 3 content. More details to be communicated very soon.
[p align="start"]Thanks to everyone who submitted questions, watched the stream, and continues to shape the game with us!

releases.displayName: Year 3 Season 1 Patch Notes

items.text: [p align="start"]Year 3 Season 1 brings the long‑awaited arrival of the Galleon to the Indian Ocean. Alongside it comes Seasonal Mastery, a rework of World Tiers, and a new iteration of Item Ascension with Mythic Modifications.
[p align="start"]So, Captain, are you ready to brave the Shattered Seas?
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/3656fb376ff03c7ac3db85640903380303f61baf.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/1551b4ea610ecde7e5fbb4a68e1156fd51d077e9.jpg"]
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]The Galleon is a DPS focused large ship with a massive number of gunports. This ship overwhelms their targets with close-range crushing firepower.
Total Gunports: 40
Broadside: 17 on each side
Bow: 4
Rear: 2
The Galleon gains a second row of lower deck weaponry.

Weapons equipped will deal 10% more weapon damage within 350m. This ship gradually charges the status 'Iron Thunder' over 1.5 seconds when it is not reloading any non-Auxiliary weapon, which increases damage dealt by 65%. 'Iron Thunder' is removed after 3 seconds on damage dealt to targets.
Allied XSML, SML and MED ships within 500m gain 10% increased damage for 30s while ‘Iron Thunder’ is active.

Increase damage dealt to targets within 250m by 35% when 'Iron Thunder' is active. On fully charging 'Iron Thunder' or upon destroying a target, confer 'Red Wake' status on your ship, which increases top speed by 50% for 15 seconds.
[p align="start"]Starting from Year 3 Season 1, the Maximum Fleet Size has been increased to 50.
[p align="start"]The new Seasonal Mastery Tree is unlocked after reaching Kingpin, where players can use their earned Infamy to increase their Seasonal Mastery Level.

[p align="start"]Each level earned provides Mastery Points which can be spent on the Mastery Skill Tree to increase various ship stats and gain Ship Rank, granting new levels of power which will be required to tackle the new World Tiers.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/8da912929e9155e351532cb0e65e85ff505d2eed.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/3ff4808f367275b24e4dfe2a8dea8320da55a9d9.jpg"]

[p align="start"]There is a total of 80 Mastery Levels to attain each season. Additionally, powerful seasonal perks will be unlocked at Mastery Levels 10, 30, 60 that can supercharge players loadouts each season.
[p align="start"]The Seasonal Journey will still be available but will focus more on guiding players through new seasonal quests and World Tiers to unlock various non-combat seasonal buffs.
[p align="start"]Both the Seasonal Mastery and Journey will reset each Season bringing with it refreshed content to both.
[p align="start"]Depending on the Mastery Levels reached at the end of each Season; players will start the next season with various levels already available.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/4b45745d826717c85b0e2f986fe9463087c5e5aa.png"]
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]Mythic Modifications are a tier of equipment modifications available for Uncommon rarity equipment and above.
Equipment can be ascended to have Mythic Modifications through the Blacksmith via Item Ascension.
Mythic Modifications can also be reforged via the Blacksmith.
[p align="start"]There is also a chance for equipment with Mythic Mods to be acquired via drops in World Tiers 3 & 4.
[p align="start"]Ascending equipment to unlock a Mythic Modification or reforging will require a new material, the Nightshade Pearl.
Nightshade Pearls can be obtained from Domains in World Tiers 3 & 4.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/d414d08f09ad21ccf708a074e71b0e4b4960a02a.png"]
[p align="start"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/ed9c3341872bc0a67aa571e84511c05c4a051f00.png"]
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]In Year 2 Season 1 we introduced World Tier 2 as we moved towards multiple levels of difficulty. With Year 3 Season 1 we’re making further improvements to the existing World Tiers and introducing new ones.

[p align="start"]Challenges have been revised and rewards redistributed. Each World Tier will offer access to increased currency and material drop rates, while simultaneously introducing new challenges in the form of Seasonal Affixes, enemy adjustments, and event availability.

[p align="start"]To unlock each new world tier, you will need to complete World Ascension quests in the previous World Tier. They work similarly to the one to unlock World Tier 2 with one exception. The Quests to unlock World Tiers 3 & 4 will be refreshed each Season and access to their targeted World Tiers rescinded.
[p align="start"]At the start of a new season, players will need to regain access to World Tiers 3 & 4 by completing the new version of each challenge quest.

[p align="start"]With the introduction of new levels of challenge, several activities have been moved to higher World Tiers to match their status as endgame challenges. We’ve also adjusted drops and rewards depending on which World Tier you play in.
\ Enemy Affixes: Affixes have been removed from Enemy Ships and Bosses in World Tier 2.
\ Seasonal & Elite Affixes: Seasonal and Elite Boss Affixes are introduced starting from this World Tier.
\ Roaming Fleets: Warships and Merchant Trade routes can now spawn in fleets instead of single ships starting from this World Tier.
Nightshade Pearls, Deep Iron and Mythic Ascended Equipment are now available as drops from Domains.
\ Mythic Bosses: The Call-to-Arm activities for La Peste (Deadly), Vikram (Deadly) and the Kraken are available in this World Tier and are now elevated to a Ship Rank of 33.
Nightshade Pearls, Deep Iron and Mythic Ascended Equipment will drop at greatly increased amounts from these Mythic Bosses.
[p align="start"]Cross server matchmaking are still available in any World Tier between 2-4.

[p align="start"]Starting from World Tier 3, enemies will now have a chance to gain a Seasonal Affix. Seasonal Affixes are a limited set of powerful abilities that replaces the existing set of randomized Affixes and now grow in strength with each additional World Tier.

[p align="start"]While Affixes are no longer applied to every ship, these limited Seasonal Affixes are much more deadly, turning even standard ships into high-threat targets that must be prioritized and strategically dealt with.
[p align="start"]These Affixes will be revised for each Season, presenting different challenges with each update.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/6eb0b84f30dd61178fa346f6e874331ee250f1b6.jpg"]

Dev Note: Right now, every ship has affixes, which means most encounters end up with too many effects happening at once. Because they are random and can have a negligible effect, they can be hard to notice or feel like they matter little during combat.

[p align="start"]With this updated system, we aim to make Affixes play a bigger and clearer role in each encounter, presenting key threats that players that are easier to spot, understand and plan around.
Increased the maximum reforge attempts of all equipment to 100.
Existing equipment will have 25 reforge attempts added after the update.
Adjusted the reforging behavior to favour modifications that have not been seen for quite some time.

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Along with increasing the number of reforge attempts to 100 with the release of Mythic Mods, we also made some adjustments to the reforge logic of item ascension. After a particular modification is seen while reforging, the chance of obtaining the same modification on the next few reforge attempts is significantly reduced.

[p align="start"]This change should allow players to more reliably obtain the specific modification combinations they want for a specific piece of equipment without running out of reforge attempts. While the chance of high/low values of modifications remain unaffected, our goal with this change is to make it easier for players to attain their preferred playstyle through their equipment modifications much earlier in the reforging process and instead spend a larger proportion of reforge attempts to perfect their modification values.
[p align="start"]We’re introducing a new Equipment Overview that gives the player the full ship’s equipment, making it easier to view and change builds.
[p align="start"]A new Ship Summary will show more information, such as visibility on how the equipment impacts your ship.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/d29732b725c3e87bd3cd06d9a13bc8cfa62d4681.jpg"]
[p align="start"]A new Layout lets players see everything at once instead of having to check items one by one.

[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/48b8f2954021916f63cffa8e490e2f82341dd9f6.jpg"]

[p align="start"]The new State of Equipment’s Tooltip gives the option to reduce the secondary stats and all visuals, making it all fit into one tooltip, which doesn’t require you to scroll. It groups related info together & prioritize important stats of each equipment.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/e5b3f75fd5a136df454da59635dd84ac3addd162.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Dev Note: Regarding the objectives mismatch, it was previously possible for players to enter into an earlier phase in their own objectives' tracker while the Megafort has already progressed. This was usually triggered via failing the objective (dying or leaving the location) or entering via backfilling.

[p align="start"]We have implemented a fix where the player’s objective will automatically progress if the objective tracker detects a mismatch. However, as this will make it possible for players to exploit the Megafort by constantly dying in the later phases to receive Phase 1 and 3’s rewards, we have moved the rewards to the end of the encounter.

Updated the Central Keep’s weakpoint activation logic to allow its north-facing weakpoints to persist after entering the final phase if they have not been destroyed earlier.
Added a new QOL functionality that disables the Megafort Wolvenhol weapons when the Central Keep’s Health falls below 0%.
The range of the Megafort Fight has also been greatly increased.

items.text: Reverted changes to Corvette handling introduced in the Y2S4.0.4 patch.
Dev Note: We’ve heard the community feedback around the Corvette feeling too light on the water when introduced in Y2S4, particularly during collisions with other ships.
In Y2S4.0.4 deployed on March 24th, we attempted to address this by making the Corvette feel heavier and closer to a Frigate in terms of handling.
Following this change, we recognize that this change was too extreme and didn’t land as intended. Based on Community feedback, we are reverting it.

We’re continuing to work on improving the Corvette’s physics and handling to find a better middle ground between it feeling too light or too heavy. This requires more investigation on our end, and will be deployed when we’re confident we have found the right solution.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/b213fe516dc62d029c2072609295aa1764647de5.jpg"]Look around Captain!
Rotting corpses, twisted ships, the DMC and Compagnie are turning these seas into a blood-soaked wasteland.
And from that cesspit, something ancient and clearly pissed off is waking. It tears every poor soul within its reach limb from limb.
But you won’t face it empty-handed.
The long-awaited Corvette finally sails into the Indian Ocean. It is your strongest chance against whatever horror is coming up from below.
And that’s only the beginning.

Year 2 Season 4 brings new seasonal buffs, new ship ranks, a fresh seasonal loadout unlocking a new playstyle, updated Faction War activities, and a wave of quality of life improvements to sharpen every captain’s edge.
So tell me, Captain… Are you ready to face the Eye of the Beast?
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/220effb0fde282369905b22ad6a034c40c1f869f.jpg"]

The Corvette sails not to steal the spotlight, but to command it. Flying its colors at the heart of the battle, this formidable warship turns every broadside into a rallying cry and every repair into renewed resolve. Enemies marked by its fire fall faster, while allies fighting beneath its banner endure longer — a true flagship for captains who win wars through coordination, pressure, and presence. If you want a sneak peek of the Corvette in action, check out our recent Deep Dive.
Ship Size: Large Ship
Archetype: Support / Broadsider
Flagbearer
For each successful shot on hostile targets, or repair on allied targets, is applied a stack of Flagbearer.
On hostile targets, each stack increases the damage dealt to the target by 1% per stack, up to 20%.
On allied targets, increases the repair received by the target by 2.5% per stack, up to 50%.
Non-hostile Extra Small, Small and Medium ships within 500m gain 5% increased damage and 5% healing amount.
Increases Hull Health restored by Repair Weapons by 5% per Repair Weapon equipped.
Upgraded Mark
At max stack of Flag mark, hostile targets will receive additional 10% weakpoint damage.
Allied targets will repair Severe damage by 1% of each incoming repair received.
Flagbearer lasts 20 seconds.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/d5ec50b90750f6cfbbeb8c63a21f9bc8fdfbf017.jpg"]Seeking only the bravest of Captains, the Kraken rises from the depths. It strikes fear in even those who are both steadfast and prepared. This is no mere sea monster. Between its immense body and far-reaching tentacles, it is a giganteum beast that towers over the Indian Ocean — leaving those wide and vast waters feeling small and insignificant in the wake of the monster's shadow.
Once the beast emerges from the depths, you will be faced with a battle shaped by your ability to withstand pressure and to adapt to unpredictable strikes.
The Kraken is now available as a World Tier 2 Call to Arms activity.
A minimum of Ship Rank 16 is required to participate.
A minimum of 3 players is required to awaken the Kraken, with a maximum of 12 players.
The Kraken features a phased fight with multiple phases of attack, and a time limit of 10 minutes.

Special Ascended equipment and the exclusive Kraken Slayer cosmetic set can be earned from completing this activity. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/4d00fd88008373e4e955ee888d7f88a4cd3b4da1.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/88c23ae133592b0e9637e59c9557b0f5102b9a38.jpg"]
The Kraken uses its tentacles and main body to unleash powerful attacks against nearby ships.
Weakpoints appear on the Kraken’s tentacles and main body throughout the fight phases and can be targeted to deal additional damage.
During specific phases, the Kraken summons whirlpools and crashing waves that disrupt ship movement.
The Kraken cleverly uses its tentacles to create vortices in the ocean, trapping ships into a spiral and dealing continuous flooding damage that increases towards the center.
The spinning tentacle in the center deals additional damage when contacted, punishing the failure to navigate away and escape.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/7d33daebbf506f616251a32c3a3913a3e3a8e029.jpg"]
"Wear the rot in your heart like a badge of honor."
Drag your enemies into the ocean’s decaying depths with the Wicked Green cosmetic set.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/ad581d6fe2b71ce487b6cd17064efa7ccbaea7be.jpg"]Join the shadowy cult of The Drowned Ones.
Claim this tentacled cosmetic set forged in the deep sea — and become a force feared by the Kraken itself.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/96b594777cd7bd2b1f029ebda6896dd2c9369e44.jpg"]Dead flames glow the brightest.
Claim the Argent Warden set and sail the seas as a warden forged in cursed silver.
We introduced the Seasonal Journey in the previous season, allowing players to unlock a variety of buffs throughout the season by exchanging excess Gildmarks.
As a new season begins, we’re kicking things off with a refreshed Seasonal Journey track, giving players a headstart on the season and even more buffs to unlock.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/5c3ce95da3df7691d7c59c70a24ae494aadfc1dc.jpg"]
We’re introducing a new way to earn rewards in-game. Players can now claim a free Daily Chest each time they log in, so be sure to check in regularly to collect your rewards.
The Daily Chest can contain a variety of rewards, including weapon chests (such as the Legacy Weapon Chest), ascension and upgrade materials, currencies, and more.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/52d51ccb1c49ddceb0ef4873e774f4abe02d7775.jpg"]The Founding returns!
Face legendary challenges and earn unique rewards as we celebrate Saint-Anne in our second year.
From 10 February 2026, 6am UTC to 10 March 2026, 6am UTC.

Complete challenges for rewards, raid Event Convoys and Sea Lord Domains to collect Silver Lions, a unique event currency that can be used at the event vendor in Sainte Anne to purchase every weapon and piece of equipment released since Year 2 Season 1.

notes.title: NEW EVENTS IN THE CONTESTED TERRITORIES

items.text: Extraction — Solo – Extract your Production of War Assets from the Contested Territory.
Manufactory Raid — Solo / Coop – Attack a Manufactory to gain War Assets and secure it for your Helm Empire.
An extraction can only be triggered at POIs you own and when producing War Assets.
The objective is to sail the War Assets through contested waters to the specified location.
Fast Travel is disabled during the run.
Navigate through enemy patrol ships and ambushes.
You must finish an extraction before you can launch another one.
Win: your produced War Assets are contributed to the territory.
Loss: the current production is lost.
A manufactory raid can happen at any POI in conflicted territories.
You can be joined by any ally.
To capture a Manufactory, you’ll need to defeat enemy ships and fill the capture bar.
As a reward, you’ll take ownership of the Manufactory and earn War Assets as a bonus.
You will only receive War Assets when successfully raiding Manufactories you already own in a Contested Territory.
Contested Territory: If the Territory is contested, the recommended Ship Rank for your assigned ship will be +1 above the usual recommendation.

Faction Victory: If your Faction controls the Territory, the effect will work in your favor. You’ll receive a 10% boost to Production Rate, and the recommended Ship Rank will be -1 below the usual recommendation.
Faction Defeat: If your Faction has lost the Territory, the effect will increase the recommended Ship Rank by +1 above the usual recommendation.

items.text: We’re introducing a quicker way to manage your ship while you’re still out at sea.
Players can now select the Manage Ship button to open the Docking Screen when close enough to a Den or Outpost, without needing to go ashore.
A new and improved pre-fire VFX has been added to AI ships.
AI attacks are now categorized into three intensity levels: Trickle, Moderate, and High, with distinct VFX representing each type.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/99692cfb9e8b97460e42199ef3b13813cfacb577.jpg"]Dev Note:

Understanding attack danger helps players make quick combat decisions. Clearer differentiation of attack intensity across ships improves communication of incoming damage and highlights Elite Warship behaviors.

This update also fixes cases where high damage ships, like Sharpshooters, used low damage VFX. These VFX improvements will roll out over multiple seasons as we update older Elite Warships to better match the intended encounter experience.
Affected Ships
Normal and stronger AI Ships
Merchant Convoys

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/38442bdafc33c395f0797cef6b0e1a36238d643f.png"]We’re adding a new quality of life feature that reduces on-screen clutter by combining the World Map, Faction War Map, and Helm Empire Map into a single widget.
This allows players to easily switch between different types of maps while staying on the same map tab.
Hulk
Ironclad (Hulk Base)

Set sail with 5 stacks of Plating and lose a stack of Plating when hull health decreases on receiving weapon hit. Each stack of Plating increases Armor Rating by 100. Gain a stack of Plating every 10 seconds. (Max 5 stacks).
Increase weapon damage by 1% per 50 total Armor Rating (Capped at 50%).

This rework shifts Hulk more firmly toward Armor Rating as its chase stat, setting it apart from other tank ships. The new Plating mechanic rewards players who Brace or Evade to maintain maximum Plating, reinforcing Hulk’s tank identity and ship size. To offset its low gunport count, Hulk now gains damage scaling from total Armor Rating, offering meaningful build-crafting options and strengthening both its durability and offensive potential.
Brig
Artificer (Brig Base)
Consecutive weapon hits targets increase weapon and repair amount by 2%, capping out at 30%. Resets if more than 11 seconds pass between hits.
Reduces Reload Time of auxiliary weapons by 10%, as well as for nearby friendly ships.
Increases Hull Health restored by Repair Weapons by 5% per Repair Weapon equipped.
Evolved (Brig Upgraded)
With non-offensive Auxiliary equipped: Restores Severe Damage by 0.4% and Brace Strength by 2% per second.
With offensive Auxiliary equipped: Increase weapon damage by 20%, as well as for nearby friendly ships.

Dev Notes: Brig was originally designed with a strong affinity for Spring Loaders, but this proved restrictive for loadout customization. We’ve taken that feedback to heart. Its base perk, Artificer, has been reworked to remove the Spring Loader dependency and now provides broader bonuses to all weapon hits and repairs. We still want Brig to embody the theme of auxiliary-weapon gameplay. To support this, the upgraded perk, Evolved, has been redesigned to scale based on the type of auxiliary weapon equipped, giving players greater freedom to tailor both perks and loadouts to their preferred playstyle.
Culverin
Reduced visual recoil on firing.
Removed damage falloff.
Long Gun
Increased visual recoil on firing.
Removed damage falloff.
Increased initial pitch of projectile fired to 2 degrees.
Dev Note: Just some minor adjustments made to further differentiate these two weapon types. We’ve also removed damage falloff to make their performance more consistent across engagement ranges.
Ballista
All Ballista Draw / Long Draw perks are removed.
New Charge Effect for all Ballista — Impale
When charged, projectile will pierce through target and deal damage based on distance travelled within the target.
Increased initial pitch of arrow fired to 2 degrees.

notes.title: All Ballista minus Twin Winch Ballista

items.text: Reduced charged multiplier from 3x to 1x.
Skyrend: Same as Impale but has the additional effect of allowing more targets to be pierced.
Adjusted “Double Draw” perk to have “Impale” perk effect.
Reduced charged multiplier from 6x to 2x.
Sea Fire
Sea Fire weapons can now be toggled on and kept on while sailing.
Reduced Idle Reload time from 3 → 2 secs.

notes.title: Increased Ammo Capacity for the following Sea Fire

items.text: Kallinikos / Blue Specter / Heavenly Thunder / Sea Fire (I, II, III) increased to 40.
Virulent Accord increased to 60.

We’re reworking both Sea Fire and Ballista to deliver more engaging, skill-based gameplay. Ballista’s long draw time often felt unrewarding when it resulted in only a single hit, so it will now deliver multiple hits to better match the commitment required. Meanwhile, Sea Fire can now be kept activated while sailing, improving visibility and offering a more flexible offensive option.

releases.displayName: Y2S3.1 Patch Notes

items.text: The Year 2 Season 3 Mid-Season Update brings new Faction War Elites events with greater War Asset rewards, the new Waterspout feature, and Inventory Management improvements amongst a number of other quality-of-life changes.
This week, the Azure Solstice also returns with new mechanics and challenges with an opportunity for you to earn exclusive cosmetics and rewards.

"Winter’s grip tightens once more as the Azure Fleet returns to haunt the ice‑choked seas. Among them sails the dreaded Azure Harbinger, a phantom of frost whose passage freezes wind and wave alike. Those who dare its icy gauntlet will find the ocean itself turned against them — yet within its hold lie treasures that only the bold can claim."
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/4919dc768ddf611068a6d97646f647f7a82f3c80.jpg"]
Azure Solstice will run 9th December 2025, 6AM UTC to 6th January 2026, 5:59AM UTC
The familiar Frostbitten Spirits Event Convoy & Azure Royale Elite Warship World Events return alongside a brand-new Elite Warship, the Azure Harbinger!
Summon the new Azure Harbinger at the event buoy using flares obtained from Event Drops, Events Quests or via the Event Vendor.
The Azure Fleet ships are protected by barriers that are vulnerable to Burning damage.
Collect Azurite and use them to get event rewards from the Event Vendor and exclusive cosmetics from the Store.
New Epic Bombard: Frostwail
New Epic Major Furniture: Sheeting Winch Console
New Event Cosmetics
Ascension materials
Ascended Weapon Chests
The Nashkar, High-Velocity Kegs, and other weapons will also be available
New Elite Warship: Azure Harbinger
New Elite Warship with unique behavior and firing patterns.
All weapons used by the Azure Harbinger can inflict a new status effect: Frostbite
Frostbite (Event-Only Status): Heavily slows down navigation and reload speed of affected ships.

Flooded Synergy - When Frostbite and Flooded are triggered at the same time, the total amount of severe damage that is done by the Flooded status will be applied instantly instead of over a period of time. Flooded will be removed after the severe damage is applied.
Ablazed Synergy - If Ablazed is triggered while Frostbite is active, the Frostbite status is removed. Players are immune to Frostbite charges when Ablazed.
Iceberg Buoy
The Azure Harbinger spawns tall, thin ice buoys in different patterns throughout the fight.
Iceberg Buoys slowly apply Frostbite charge to all nearby players.
Ice Crystal Buoy
The Azure Harbinger spawns small, round ice buoys in different patterns throughout the fight.
Ice Crystal Buoys explode after a short buildup, dealing damage to nearby players.
Armor of Frost
At fixed health thresholds, the Azure Harbinger activates a special barrier that cannot be destroyed by any weapons.
Destroy the crystal figurehead weakpoint of the Elite Warship to break the barrier.
If the Armor of Frost is not destroyed after a fixed period of time, the Elite Warship will heal for a portion of its health

notes.title: NEW FACTION WAR EVENT: FACTION WAR ELITE

items.text: “The tides of war surge as the corporations unleash their most fearsome leviathans yet. The Mighty Opwelling and Mighty Soleil Imperial thunder into battle, each armed with devastating new technologies. Only the bold will face their volatile fury and berserker rage — but victory promises War Assets enough to turn the course of the conflict.”
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/5c717ab4ca42adf12de9fe0b439f31c8eba61787.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/cde1f3fef030861c76718b888e45032317f1e6cf.jpg"]
The Opwelling and Soleil Royal elite warships return in War Events as the Mighty Opwelling and Mighty Soleil Imperial, featuring dangerous new affixes that make them even greater threat than before.
Take down these Flagships in the new Faction War Elite Events to earn large amounts of War Assets for the war effort!
New War Event: Faction War Elite
Mighty Opwelling (DMC)
Mighty Soleil Imperial (Compagnie)

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/713464d451c79abe39e996fd64ba9ba4c68cdd27.png"]

“The seas now hold a new predator — swirling towers of wind and wave. Master their power to sling your ship across the horizon in a surge of speed… or twist their fury into a trap for your foes. Will you dance with the storm, or feed your enemies to it?”
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/7ce8ac3c078ff96836f939b7cac4a663d64a428d.jpg"]

Waterspouts are a new type of weather phenomena which provides seasoned captains with new navigational challenges. Skilled captains can ride the current for a burst of speed and slingshot across the water.
When approaching a waterspout, sail along the outer radius to gain a significant movement speed bonus in the direction of the wave.
Sailing too close to the eye of the waterspout will however pull your ship inwards towards the waterspout and damage your sails – so approach with care.
Clever maneuvering can also lure enemy ships into a waterspout, trapping them long enough for you to escape or land a powerful mortar shot on multiple clustered targets.

Dev Note: We know this has been a long-requested feature from the community and we’re excited to finally bring this to you. While this was initially slated for a later release while being applied to wider range of menus, we wanted to bring this change to you as soon as possible and so we’ve first targeted the most commonly used menus. We’ll continue to refine this and gradually apply it to other menus in the future.
Added filter tabs for inventory categories across various menu screens
Ship Loadouts

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/cf0e5676c1163592e56f2fbc4e988fd4564ad270.png"]

War Cargo

Disabled Fast Travel while participating in the activity

Dev Note: This adjustment aims to ease early-game frustration for players using smaller ships. The goal is to ensure new players do not form the mistaken impression that small ships are inherently weaker, but instead understand their role and potential as they learn the game’s systems.
All quadrants are now unlocked by default for small ships
Small ships no longer need to be upgraded to unlock rear gunports.
Adjusted small ships upgrades to account for this change.
Dev Note: We’re increasing the amount of taunt generated to make the Frigate perform slightly better in its intended tank role.
Increased the amount of taunt generated by the Frigate’s perk.
Dev Note: We’re renaming Boarding to Crew Finisher, streamlining the flow to not break immersion, and unlocking the camera to make this a more comfortable alternative to simply sinking ships.
Boarding is now renamed to Crew Finisher.
Success conditions have been improved.
The boarding cinematic and the loot screens have been removed.
The camera is no longer locked to the cinematic.
No changes to bonus loot for boarding.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/ffb3b8407028cddc85e030e522e1f39a4def0dbe.gif"]

Dev Note: We’re aware that the last set of changes to character navigation didn’t land as well as we’d thought it would. We’re making slight improvements to reduce the “floatiness” and desynchronization of character animations especially during sharp turns and during the starting and ending movement animations.
Adjusted land character navigation.

Dev Note: Inventory Management continues to be our highest quality-of-life priority. In addition to the increase of cargo slots we introduced a few weeks ago, and on top of the new filter tabs feature in this patch, we’re making smaller, targeted improvements to ease top areas of friction. We’re still studying and working on ways to further improve the topic of Inventory Management. Do let us know what you would like to see next!
Multiple items (including Ascended Equipment) can now be marked for salvage at the Blacksmith.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/7c6de8594d274f756f29442cc5a5d3e69a2d7c8b.jpg"]
All chest types now support opening multiple chests of the same type simultaneously.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/af42cd72a9423e54d4a963a3d7650d5a5826f794.jpg"]
Improved item selection logic when equipping/unequipping items to your ship
Fast Travel now allows you to choose between going on land, like usual, or staying at sea.
Approaching or joining World Events will no longer automatically replaces the Objective Tracker.
Added an option for players to Hold to Track when approaching or joining a World Event to replace the contents of the Objective Tracker
Pressing the back button on the Logbook navigation no longer closes the entire Logbook but returns players to the previous screen.
Improved readability of text in the death screen.
Renamed “Craft New Items” to “Craft Ships” in the Shipwright menu for clarity.
Removed duplicated “Missing Ingredients” error message when crafting a ship.
Readjusted the priority and order of appearances of some notifications.
Added Ship Rank and number of participants to World Event iconography in the world map.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/067fc423de2890f99b4846d3d3e667cbee08290a.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45116157/366e2a09495eab8b15b0e844fc45ed985bec3428.jpg"]

Dev Note: Since the launch of Year 2 Season 3, we’ve improved our anti-spam monitoring tools which allow us to systematically detect and ban text chat abusers on a daily schedule. We’ve seen a significant decrease of text chat abuse, but we’re doing one more change to address this issue. We’ve assessed the impact of this change for new players to be minimal if they’re actively progressing in the onboarding campaign.
Increased the minimum Infamy needed to interact with Text Chat to 4
Improved the onboarding flow for new players
Objectives for new players are now more focused
Added Call-For-Help Tutorial
Updated initial repair kits obtained from S to M
Updated equip step to reach SR level
Removed forced “Look at” encounters
Removed blockade on the final encounter
Increased Fara Scout difficulty (swapped to a hard ship variant)
Update objective texts to bring focus to Compagnie merchants
Increase ship rank of Compagnie Flagship
Tier 1 weapons removed from Onboarding
Added a panel at the end of the onboarding flow highlighting latest opportunities in Endgame.
Added a closing cinematic for the Year 3 Seasonal 3 Seasonal Journey with the St Anne Blacksmith.
Improved the ambience of Mythic La Peste and Mythic Vikram World Events
La Peste’s Mythic Event now features visuals with darker storm clouds, green ambient lighting, drifting poison ash, and a distinct green aura to enhance the atmosphere.
The second phase of Vikram Rajan’s Mythic Event with darker storm clouds and yellow ambient lighting to heighten the fight’s atmosphere.
Key NPCs now track your approach and turn to face you when you get close, making interactions feel more responsive and alive.
Year 2 Seasonal 3 has been extended to 16 weeks, and now ends on 10 February 2026, 06:00 UTC.
Faction War will still end on Week 14, with an extended, two-week ceasefire from Week 15 to Week 16 in preparation for Year 2 Season 4.
Dev Note: Long queue times have been an issue for Death Tides for some time now. We’re making a quick change to get players into matches faster.
Adjusted the match size for all game modes, maps, and matches to 3v3

Dev Note: Since our previous communication where we mentioned we would be prioritizing stability, we’ve made significant progress in investigating and resolving a myriad of issues which were proven to or could potentially lead to lower stability health. We’re continuing to investigate and resolve rarer causes of instability and will release any improvements whenever they are tested and ready.
Improved Client, Network, and Server stability
