releases.displayName: Y2S3 Patch Notes

items.text: In the latest Season of Skull and Bones, the Indian Ocean becomes a battleground as the war between the Dutch Merchant Company and Compagnie Royale intensifies, turning trade routes into perilous zones of conflict. Amidst this chaos, there are rumors of the Plague King's resurgence. Once thought lost to the sea, returns with a formidable fleet armed with forbidden weaponry, spreading the Drowning Plague that silences ports and swallow ships in fog.

[p align="start"]Pirates and local factions alike are caught in a storm of loyalty versus profit, with the new Sloop-of-War emerging as a coveted asset among Philippe La Peste's fleet, designed for swift attacks. Meanwhile, the region's blacksmiths have reverse-engineered these advanced weapon schematics to craft powerful armor, hinting at the involvement of a shadowy arms dealer.
[p align="start"]As tensions rise, opportunities for power and riches beckon those daring enough to seize them, albeit at a high price.

[p align="start"]Medium in size and monstrous in appetite, this Poison DPS vessel is built for the slow burn---turning Toxic weapons into instruments of attrition and victory into a lingering sting. With Ship Perks Plaguebringer and Spite at its core, it deepens the venom, spreads the malaise, and turns proximity into peril, rewarding captains who savor corrosion over concussion. Take the helm, let the poison do the talking, and watch your enemies wilt.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/4ZYrD2B4KfoxLFTUvK7AbK/a3bb12c8eceb7f3d275317bb511f5dc2/SLOOP_OF_WAR.jpg"]
Size: Medium
Archetype: DPS (Poison)
A DPS focused ship that excels at dealing damage over time and is especially efficient in combat with Toxic weapons.
Plaguebringer

When attacking a target under Poisoned status effect, it increases the damage and duration of the Poisoned status effect by 6% and 20% respectively for each consecutive hit up to 30% increased damage and 100% increased duration. Weapon hit has a chance to cause a poison explosion of 300m on the target, dealing 1000 Toxic damage to hostile enemies.
Increase Toxic Weapons damage by 20% and Poisoned charge up rate by 150%.
Spite

When attacking a target under the Poisoned status effect, the target will deal 50 Toxic Damage per second to nearby hostiles within 300m for 10 seconds. It decreases weapon damage received from the targets under Poisoned status effect by 30%.

[p align="start"]Turn the tides of the Faction War as the 2 factions wrestle for territorial control over the Indian Ocean each season in a series of contested zones. Every few weeks, a new battle phase is introduced - attack rival forces in Contested Zones and accumulate War Assets for your chosen faction.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/4EZnQrj24MsoNx0J9GKZwh/f71a0cedc9e09b4c9bd1f7017a1daf1d/FACTION_WAR.jpg"]
Conquer the most Territories as a faction within the season to win the war.
Every few weeks, 2 to 5 Territories will become contested Territories. The faction that collects the most War Assets in this Territory at the end of the Battle Phase wins control of it.
Sinking enemies or Plundering settlements in Contested Territories.
War Convoy - A convoy from the enemy transports a large amount of War Assets. Pillage them to secure War Assets for your faction.
Fort Defense - Join forces and defend the fort against an enemy assault to secure War Assets for your faction.
War Cargo (1v1 PVP) - Find and deliver the drifting War Assets to their destination. Fight anyone who gets in your way!
[p align="start"]The number of Contested Territories during each battle phase escalates as the Season progresses, with a total of 21 Territories to be contested.
[p align="start"]Faction War: Year 2 Season 3
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/2EKmZk0ZFrwrGhoIahJc7d/b809ff2b6518862e5dfe6b012243e379/War_Timeline_Updated.png"]
[p align="start"]Please note the timeline is subject to change and only applicable to Year 2 Season 3.

notes.title: Contribute War Assets as part of the war effort to unlock

items.text: Exclusive Weapons & Furniture.
Curated Ascended Weapons.
Valuable materials & other rewards.
Capture Territories with your Faction to unlock a Faction exclusive ship set.
Seasonal Faction War reward - the winning Faction will unlock a Captain Vanity set.
Heavenly Thunder (Sea Fire)
Lancer: Fires a streak of lightning that can chain up to 4 targets in proximity. Increases damage by 1% per 10m of Weapon Range. Adds 75m to Weapon Range.
Electric III: Adds 30% of damage as Electric Damage.
Burning I: Adds 10% of damage as Burning Damage.
Virulent Accord (Sea Fire)
Infectious: Hitting the same target 8 times deals 13% Toxic Damage to nearby enemies within 150m, Weapon Damage increases by 1% for each subsequent hit on the same target.
Toxic III: Adds 30% of damage as Toxic damage.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/2llUJdpeGnoSZ5NKA5Uh44/c2a7a5c1f41cc99fec04b58ae8f50792/Sea_Fire_Weapons.jpg"]
For every 5m Area-of-effect Radius of the weapon, it increases weapon damage as Electric Damage by 2%.
Reduces Reload Time of Electric Weapons by 6%.
Increases damage to enemy ships with the Stormstruck effect by 8%.
Increases weapon damage of Sea Fire by 13%.
Increases Secondary Damage of Sea Fire by 7%.
Increases Charge Rate of the Poisoned status effect on a target by 8%.
Increases duration of the Poisoned effect on enemy ships by 8%.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/6taKbo9z0oxEZ9vJjZLToE/ad9c9275ce4db241cc94bd28c7fac966/FURNITURE.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Season 3 will be introducing a new seasonal ecosystem to the game, with the goal of giving players easy access to all currently available events, store offers and engagement systems on one single screen.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/24cwK9jHGF3o7iqZTVvGRP/ad8edefc2807f63cac8a8a9c3e0b7322/SeasonalLandingPage_Final.jpg"]

[p align="start"]The Seasonal Hub will be the main portal for players to check out the key events and features of each Season. Browsing each entry will show a brief overview and selecting it will bring you to their respective details and menus. Upcoming Events will also appear on the Seasonal Hub keeping you up to date of what's to come!
The Seasonal Journey allows players to progress by completing specific contracts and tasks.
The Journey provides buffs for the duration of the season.
This Journey and its accompanying buffs will be reset at the end of each season.
New quests can be unlocked by further progression through the Seasonal Journey.
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/1Z0WSYcB28COiC26ZQeDB1/79a80987d2ad31ded4040014ffe68738/SEASONAL_JOURNEY_BUFFS.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Set sail for the Domains---uncharted waters where Sea Lord factions reign and legends stir beneath the wake. Seek out signal buoys, stock the right lures, and bait the titans into the open---from La Peste and the Hubac Twins to Zamaharibu and the Rode Maangodin---then carve your name across all World Tiers. Prove your infamy, complete your rite of passage, and the map will grant swift passage to the next hunt. Call them out, cut them down, and let the sea remember you.

[p align="start"]Domains are regions where players engage with Sea Lord factions and summon their Elites to battle. Buoys scattered across these territories can be activated to call forth the Elites---each requiring specific items to awaken them at their respective locations.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/LaCJ4xuqUZ1wjG58eXazV/b09e780df6968255ce281a0f7dce71e4/DOMAINS.jpg"]
Sea Lord Buoys (La Peste, Hubac Twins, Li Tian Ning & Vikram Rajan) are summoned by Flares which can be collected from sinking their minions in the Domains or purchased from Blackwood.
Sea monsters (Zamaharibu, Mega Lestari, Shadowbeast) can be summoned from their Domain Buoys with Monstrous Bait that can be purchased from the vendor in Lanitra.
The Rode Maangodin can be summoned from its Domain Buoy with Essence of Spirits that can be purchased from the vendor in Forgotten Candi.
Domains are available across all World Tiers.

notes.title: Prerequisites for fast travelling via map marker

items.text: Infamy level 10.
Must have defeated all the Sea Lords such as La Peste, Hubac Twins, Li Tian Ning, Vikram Rajan, Sea Monsters and Rode Maangodin.
Completed the onboarding contract for Domains.

[p align="start"]Armor Ascension has arrived---take your plating from sturdy to legendary. Forge new strength at the Blacksmith or hunt down pre-ascended pieces in the wild, then stack up to four upgrades across three grades to tailor your defenses for the voyage ahead. Slot potent mods that harden your hull, sharpen your bracing, steady your stamina, and shrug off the elements. Each ascension level amplifies your armor rating, keeping you in the fight through the fiercest squalls. Build a bulwark, bend the storm, and let your armor be the edge that outlasts everything.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/1JWbfgN4KpnmZ8zeG552Ay/78875ec7cb308f339b209d4fceefdc8f/ARMOR_ASCENSION.jpg"]
Ascend armor at the Blacksmith or acquire pre-ascended armor via loot in the world.
Like Weapon Ascension, Armor Ascension allows players to build up to 4 upgrades across 3 grades of modifications that improve survivability.
Modification slots get added to the armor when it gets ascended.
Each Ascension level adds +5% armor rating to a given armor.
1 ascension level -> +5% armor rating.
2 ascension levels -> +10% armor rating.
3 ascension levels -> +15% armor rating.
4 ascension levels -> +20% armor rating (Common armor only).
[p align="start"]The following modifications are available in the Armor Ascension rolls by Grade:
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/2nGfDnNFHbft59d7YWGkdv/cad221947a4db878cf7aaccf8ae8dd8f/Armour_Mods_Basic.jpg"]
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/1FoMmZsata9ciEPAvVA71k/115dfbe9e9f5a86766dc5d5c75fa18e7/Armour_Mods_Advanced.jpg"]
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/5hHWa0cRy7sDnBLvPbFEsc/19ac63c32daa9348abc9763a463e5cd1/Armour_Mods_Expert.jpg"]
Your ship will now be repaired automatically when docked.
This function can be toggled on/off from the "Set Sail" screen. This function is Off by default.
Silver cost for repairing ships remain unchanged.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/6LoaqDkKuurWYSt9HjGQDC/b35d2f6435fcb05a8c3700a90a53780f/AUTOMATIC_REPAIR.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Toxic rises as a new secondary damage type - seeping into crews, sapping stamina, and swelling toward the Poisoned status: a creeping malady that makes bracing feel brittle and every heartbeat count. Signature kits like La Piqûre, Le Fléau, and Wrathful Ward now carry the sting, while new weapon mods lace your shots with a noxious bite---or temper the venom to taste.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/tYkewBeOxPRJdvejIVHIT/0da27cb032820590944d9dfe38dbd446/TOXIC_DAMAGE.jpg"]
[p align="start"]Choose your cure or double down on the disease---either way, your broadside is about to bite.
Toxic secondary damage type is now formally a damage type consistent with other secondary damage types (e.g. Burning, Flooding, etc.).
1% of any Toxic damage dealt drains Crew Stamina from target.
Toxic Damage will build up and trigger the Poisoned Status Effect.
The following weapons and armor have been retroactively adjusted to utilize the new Toxic damage type:
La Piqûre
Le Fléau
Wrathful Ward
Upon applying sufficient Toxic secondary damage on a target, the Poisoned status effect will be triggered.

The Poisoned status effect deals between ~175-230 base damage per second vs player targets, depending on the maximum health of the target. Against AI targets this number can grow higher, as they can have significantly higher maximum health.

While affected by Poisoned status effect, target's Brace Mitigation is reduced by 50%. Example: Ship A is poisoned. It receives a hit of 1000 damage - 500 is absorbed by Brace Strength, the remaining 500 will apply to the target's Hull Health
While affected by Poisoned status effect, Bracing consumes 60% more Crew Stamina than normal.
A balance pass has also been made to existing armors and ships to include Toxic resistance.
[p align="start"]The following weapon mods have been added to complement the new damage type.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/y4nbYUXJftAfXo40YYMAS/b215c8f3fd962af50883d19dc36c0410/Weapon_Mods.jpg"]
[p align="start"]The following affixes have been added to the pool of possible affixes for enemies in World Tier 2:
Blessing of Toxic
When rammed, this ship takes additional 500% Ram Damage When this ship receives Toxic Damage, its Hull Health is repaired by 7 of the Secondary Damage Taken.
Poisoned Resistant
Reduces Incoming Toxic Charge from enemy ships by 10%.

[p align="start"]La Peste returns stronger than ever, beckoning the bravest captains to the sickly-green horizon. Veterans will find this symphony decidedly venomous; lesser vessels may find the waters a little... toxic.

[p align="start"]This is a fight that loves to linger in your veins: its signature venom mirrors the new Poisoned status---gnawing over time, biting harder the more you let it build, slipping fangs past your best defenses, and spreading to the unwary who huddle too close.

[p align="start"]Keep your distance, keep your cool, and don't let the pressure poison your judgment. The plague-ship calls---answer wisely, and you'll leave the sea feeling contagious... with triumph.
[p align="start"][img src="https://staticctf.ubisoft.com/J3yJr34U2pZ2Ieem48Dwy9uqj5PNUQTn/1Fd2oG4aoAdep3Nn2LqkkA/14d0c9c29375f756ef9483a8121e4456/MYTHIC_LA_PESTE__1_.jpg"]
Mythic La Peste is now available as a permanent Call-to-Arms activity, alongside Mythic Vikram and Megafort Wolvenhol.
A minimum Ship Rank requirement of SR12 is needed to initiate Call-To-Arms.
The encounter introduces poison-focused mechanics aligned with the new Poisoned status effect, including contagious toxins that can spread to nearby players.
Special Ascended equipment with an increased chance of poison-related modifiers can be earned from this activity.

[p align="start"]The Character Suit is a new vanity type for characters, and players can find this new category while customizing their captain in the Atelier. Equipping the character suit will override the vanity visuals of other character vanity slots.

[p align="start"]Dev note: With the introduction of Faction War, we've taken the opportunity to review the existing hostility rules. These changes aim to improve the pacing of combat escalation, while simultaneously improving its readability by introducing a new set of reinforcements.
Added Minimum Ship Rank requirement of SR12 to initiate Call-To-Arms.

[p align="start"]Dev note: While we continue exploring more permanent solves to players who do not contribute to activities, we're first introducing this requirement to ensure that participants adopt an appropriate loadout for the encounter.

All status effects (Ablaze, Flooded, Punctured, Shellshocked, Stormstruck, Poisoned) are now consistently applied to towers; previously, only a few were supported, and their application was inconsistent.
Added Minimum Ship Rank requirement of SR12 to initiate Call-To-Arms.
[p align="start"]In our efforts to streamline item management in Skull and Bones, we will be removing some items that are not commonly used and unnecessarily cluttering inventory space.
26 items are no longer obtainable from the game, from loot sources, vendors and buyout features.
Manufactory and refinery production of the affected materials that was funded prior to the start of Season 3 will be cancelled - the production cost will be refunded respectively.
Existing crafting recipes have been adjusted accordingly with the removal of the affected materials.
Existing materials will not be removed from your inventories. These items can be converted to other usable materials at the Refinery or sold for silver at vendors.

items.text: With the impending arrival of Faction Wars, we're evolving the world to reflect the next chapter in your journey. As players transition from World Tier 1 to World Tier 2, the world itself will shift to reflect the aftermath of Year 1's story and the re-emergence of the Schaduw and the Artifact.
Gold on her hull, fire in her lungs
Steel in her belly, where judgment is sung...
Armand Hubac: Let cowards flee and traitors swing---: Long live Le Firmament. Long live the King.

Bertrand Hubac: Unveiled as the beacon of the Sun King's might, Le Firmament is a large warship bristling with advanced weaponry. As the Compagnie strikes back against the DMC incursion into the Red Isle, pirates bold enough may claim this vessel to turn the tide of war.: Large sized, Tank: Dual Auxiliary Weapon - Your equipped Auxiliary weapon now has 2 stations: Devastating Firepower - Up to 34 gun ports in total when using culverins.: Vast Cargo Hold - Haul all that loot with a massive Weight Limit starting at 80,000: Immense Durability - 100,000 Hull Health at Ship Upgrade 1 and up to 128,400 Hull Health at Ship Upgrade 7: Unwavering Stability - Stands firm against the tide and waves. Making it easier to aim.: Rear Weapon Dead Zones - Serious firepower comes with trade-off, in between the rear quadrants are some dead zones where weapons are unable to fire at.: Multiple Weak points - Big target, bigger threat - master positioning to dominate. *These weak points are only exploitable on PVP.
A ship that excels with its robust defenses and radiates a powerful aura that fortifies allies, embodying its tank role with unmatched resilience.
Gain a stack of Grit when you take damage. Each stack of Grit increases Armor by 40, up to maximum of 10 stacks. Each stack of Grit lasts 15 secs.
Extra small, Small & Medium ships within 200m take 10% reduced damage. If you have 10 Stacks of Grit, Allied ships take 20% reduced damage instead.
Upgrade the Frigate to unlock Secondary Perk: Resolve
At 10 stacks of Grit, taking damage grants you Resolve. Resolve restores 10% Brace Strength on activate, decreases status effect damage by 20% and increases threat generation by 100% for 10 seconds
Dev Note: Frigates are designed to play and feel massive, commanding, and impossible to ignore. Though slow to maneuver, they unleash devastating firepower, acting as both a shield and a spear.

Obtaining a ship of this class and power is no easy feat requiring hard to obtain materials such as Deep Iron to craft. While working towards Tier 45 of the Smuggler Pass for the blueprint, a wise Captain can start gathering Deep Iron from the new Megafort Wolvenhol or purchasing them regularly from William Blackwood.
Want to learn more about Large Ships and the Frigate, check out the Large Ships DevBlog.
You want to test your mettle, pirate? Come knock on our gates. See if your bark survives our bite.

Jonas Vanderkill: Anchored in the heart of the Red Isle, Megafort Wolvenhol is a fortress bristling with guns, galleys, and grim resolve. Only the most daring of pirate crews will breach the walls of the Wolf-Hunter... or die trying.: Form an alliance with other captains to face the high-pressure mission of taking down the new Megafort Wolvenhol and earn rewards that will aid you in upgrading the Frigate! The Megafort is also a treasure trove of materials such as Ascension materials, Masterwork Kits, Upgrade parts, and more!: To challenge the new Megafort Wolvenhol, all players need to be in World Tier 2. From the Journal, visit the Events tab, search for the 'Indian Ocean Activities' header and select "The Wolves' Hollow". Use the "Call to Arms" function to start the event. A total of 6 Captains minimum are required to start the event, up to 20 players. Take down the new Megafort within the time limit of 30 minutes to succeed.: Upon the successful take down of the Megafort, participants will be rewarded with: Masterwork Kit: Upgrade Part: Ascension Modules: Pieces of Eight and Silver: A Megafort Cache containing Specialized Materials, Refined Helm materials and a random Ascended Weapon

We've made significant improvements to the core sailing experience, bringing it closer to the real-world dynamics of wind and sea. These changes are designed to give you more control, more depth, and more ways to sail like a true captain.
Different sail types now interact uniquely with wind direction:
Mastering the right sail for the conditions is now a crucial part of your strategy.
[table equalcells="1" colwidth=","]
Square Sails Brigantine, Frigate, Snow, Cutter etc Rectangular sails perpendicular to the ship
Lateen Sails Padewakang, Sambuk, Bedar etc Triangular sails parallel to the ship
Upwind will cause a brief speed reduction when sailing upwind.
Upwind will have little to no speed reduction (briefly) when sailing upwind.
Sails rotation to optimal sails angle is narrower. (Time taken to adjust to wind direction is shorter)
Sails rotation to optimal sails angle is wider. (Time taken to adjust to wind direction is longer)
Sailing with Downwind will have bonus speed.
Sailing with Downwind will not have bonus speed.
Stamina consumption has been updated to better reflect the rhythm of sailing:
Initial Acceleration: Trimming the sails will cause a short burst of stamina drain as your ship picks up speed.
Optimal Trim Speed: Once you're cruising, stamina consumption is significantly reduced, allowing for longer voyages.
Downwind Sailing: Trimming costs are greatly reduced, making it the most efficient direction for conserving stamina.
Neutral Winds: Trimming drains stamina at a standard rate.
Upwind Sailing: Trimming causes a brief spike in stamina drain before stabilizing as the ship adjusts.
With the introduction of the Frigate, it became clear to us that we wanted you to truly feel the weight of the ship and so we revisited how ships handled based on their inherent mobility and mass.
Momentum: Ships now preserve more of their momentum when dropping anchors allowing advanced maneuvers allowing for tighter turns, allowing you to better outmaneuver your enemies.

Different ship sizes have different ranges of maneuverability, allowing players to decide what best fits their individual playstyles - from nimble hit-and-run tactics to hulks that crush everything in its path.
Small ships: Allows for fast turn rates even at high speeds
Medium ships: Moderate turn rates at high speed
Large ships: Slow turn rates at high speeds

Take advantage of Wind Gust Zones scattered across the Indian Ocean to gain temporary speed boosts. Skilled navigation and timing will let you ride the wind to outmaneuver enemies, reach objectives faster, or simply enjoy the thrill of high-speed sailing.
These changes reward smart sailing and give you more ways to manage your crew's endurance during long journeys or intense chases.

With the impending arrival of Faction Wars, the world is evolving, reflecting the next chapter in your journey. As players transition from World Tier 1 to World Tier 2, the world itself will shift to reflect the aftermath of Year 1's story and the re-emergence of the Schaduw and the Artifact.

World Tier 1 now represents the Year 1 world state, including all Year 1 Main Story Quests for players to catch up on our game's story, explore the Indian Ocean, and get familiar with the key tactics of sailing and naval combat.
World Tier 2 introduces a transformed Indian Ocean, setting the stage for Faction Wars and continuing the narrative with Year 2 Main Story Quests and Seasonal Quests.

Dev Note: These changes are a first step towards a more streamlined and narratively coherent experience. With the introduction of World Tiers 2, we've heard your feedback about the world feeling overcrowded, with overlapping events and unpredictable difficulty spikes.

Our goal is first to ensure all players have more control over the type of experience they want, ensuring the difficulty scaling feels progressive, intentional and rewarding, and giving the world a structure that grows as you progress through the game's story.
We've also heard about your concerns about the community being separated between new and veteran players. This is a topic the team is actively looking into addressing in a future update.
The availability of activities has been categorized (and split) between World Tier 1 and 2 to streamline the number of activities available for each World Tier.
To ensure continuity and flexibility, Infamy Quests, Side Quests, Job Board Contracts, Bounties, Helm Contracts, and Time-Limited Event Quests will remain available in both World Tiers.
All regular World Events will be on permanent rotation in World Tier 1:
Elite Warships (Vanderkill, Opwelling, Soleil Royal, Commander Zhang, Mizerja, Rode Maangodin)
Seasonal Pirate Lords (Vikram Rajan, Li Tian Ning, The Hubac Twins, La Peste)
Sea Monsters (Shadowbeast, Mega Lestari, Risen Mega Lestari, Zamaharibu, Risen Zamaharibu).
Dangerous variants of World Events will be exclusive to World Tier 2, reflecting the heightened stakes and evolving threats of the new world state:
Elder Shadowbeast
Phillipe La Peste (Dangerous)
The Hubac Twins (Dangerous)
Li Tian Ning (Dangerous)
Vikram Rajan (Dangerous)
Vikram Rajan (Deadly) - introduced in World Tier 1, only playable after World Tier 2 is unlocked via World Ascension Quest
Players can check the Seasonal Calendar to stay updated on active events in World Tier 2.

The availability of World Events will remain dynamically scheduled in World Tier 2 with different content throughout the season to keep activities in the Indian Ocean refreshed. The in-game Seasonal Calendar will reflect current and upcoming key events in World Tier 2,

items.text: Captains, a Skull and Bones maintenance is incoming 🛠️
🗓️ Tuesday 27th May
⏰8AM CEST / 4PM AET / (26 MAY) 11PM PT
🔧 Update Y2S1.1 will be deployed. Read the full Patch Notes below ⬇️
Death Tides, Skull and Bones’ long-awaited dedicated PvP game mode, is here!
Along with the release of Death Tides, this mid-season update brings to players balance changes, quality-of-life improvements, bugfixes, and stability improvements.
Players will need to finish the Main Game’s Introductory Sequence in order for Death Tides to be visible in the Main Menu.
To access Death Tides from the Journal in the Indian Ocean, players will need to finish the “Into the Lion’s Den” and “Death Tides” contracts.
You may select up to 5 ships from your own fleet to participate in Death Tides! You can also do this through the Docking Screen > Manage Ship screen in the Indian Ocean.
Each ship can be assigned 1 PvP ultimate as part of the ship customization to be used in Death Tides game modes (read more about Ultimates below).
Still building up your dream fleet? Not to worry, there are 6 pre-fitted loadouts for players to jump into PvP immediately:
All Preset ships are set by default at Ship Upgrade 7
DPS-focused: Disruptor (Sloop), Pyrocast (Sambuk) and Lancelot (Bedar), Marksman (Garuda)
Support-focused: Paladin (Barque)
Tank: Stormwall (Battle Junk)

While participating in Death Tides, you may encounter power-ups around the map that grants the individual a temporary boost. Sail over the power ups to gain short-term advantages such as increased speed and damage, or simply to recover some hull health.
Upon picking up the power-ups, you are instantly granted one of the following:
+30% Damage for 20s.
+70% sailing speed for 25s and recover stamina by 60%.
Repair all severe hull damage, recover stamina by 60% and Regenerates 6000 health points every 2 seconds for 15s.
When you are sunk, you get the opportunity to select another ship to use or stick to your guns should you choose to!
Repair Kits are available in Death Tides but only limited to 1 at a time - 1 granted on respawn.
Each time a player spawns, you’ll obtain a Death Tides specific Repair Kit.
Severe damage is fully repaired upon respawning.
Crew attacks are not usable in Death Tides.
Repair kits and food from your Inventory do not work in Death Tides.

Different pre-fitted ships have different types of Ultimates associated with them. Try all sorts of ships and their abilities! Charge your Ultimate to activate an Ultimate that is assigned to each ship to give you or your team an advantage during combat.
Ultimate Charge builds up passively over time, but can be accelerated by:
Dealing damage
Receiving damage
Sinking opponents
Healing teammates
Choose from 11 Ultimates to assign to each of 5 ships that you’ve chosen from your own fleet.

Power Weapons are temporary weapons that are automatically equipped onto your ship when activated. Once equipped, you have the option to choose when you want to fire these weaponries. When you run out of ammunition, the weapons will be automatically unequipped, and your original weapons will return.
Combat Skills apply temporary benefits
Bastion: Confers a moment of invulnerability
Combat Fury: Increase damage dealt, heals hull and Stamina
Summon a Legendary entity that will support your team in fighting your enemy
In Team-Based modes, each team is limited to one legendary summon at a time.
The health of Legendary entities will be depleted over time.
Based on individual (deaths, kills, damage, point capture, assists etc.) + team stats (score and win/loss), each player will receive up to a maximum of 1000 Infamy.
All participants will receive some specialized material, Seasonal Currency, Smuggler points and Silver.
Winner’s Bonus: Additional Specialized material, Seasonal Currency and Silver.
Kingpin Bonus:
Winning team will receive a Gold Raider Cache each
The losing team will receive a Silver Raider Cache each
Participating in matches will grant you PvP XP. Accumulate PvP XP to earn additional ships and equipment to aid you in your rise in notoriety in the Indian Ocean.
Tidebreaker: A 6v6 PVP game mode – be the first team to capture and defend a zone to gain victory points.
Out of 5 capture zones, only 1 zone will be active (i.e. available for capture) at any point in time.
Once the active point has been captured an announcement will be made, stating the next active point and the amount of time it is active will be made.

Establish control and capture the active zone to gain points. More players of the same team within the zone increases the progress rate of capturing the zone. Beware! If there are less teammates contesting the control point, the opposing team will continue to make progress in capturing the control point – even if there is one teammate contesting the control point!
Each successful capture gives the 1 Victory point. The first team to reach 3 points wins.
If teams are tied at the end of the timer, the game enters Sudden Death, and the next team to capture a zone wins.
Fleetfire: A pure PVP game mode that pits 2 teams consisting of 3 or 6 players against each other - sink your opponents to gain victory points!
Each opponent sunk earns you 1 Victory Point
In 3v3 Fleetfire matches, the first team to reach 15 points wins.
In 6v6 Fleetfire matches, the first team to reach 23 points wins.
Alternatively, by the end of 15 minutes, the team with the highest score wins.
If there is a tie at the end of 15 minutes, the game will enter Sudden Death - the next kill wins the match!
For more details on the new Death Tides mode, check out the Death Tides Deep Dive.

Dev Note: With the release of Death Tides, balancing becomes an even more important topic to ensure match fairness and variety of builds. We continue to recognize the need for regular balance changes and have made some changes in response to feedback from internal testing and the Insider Program.

Moving forward, we will be aiming to make regular balance changes, where we release adjustments based on analyzed data and collected player sentiment. This new process and balancing cadence will help us to accurately quantify the impact of our changes through extensive internal testing, and at the same time provide predictability and time for players to adjust to new builds and adapt to the meta.
As we collect more data from the public release of Death Tides, please continue to provide your feedback through the usual social media channels.
La Piqure I, II, III: Reduced the stamina drain from the Toxic perk from 15 to 7

Dev Note: The Poison Long Guns have been adjusted for PVP previously a single salvo could take away most a player’s stamina. This effectively reduced their ability to brace which was detrimental to tank builds.
Shell-shocked: Disables the ship’s ability to fire its weapons. The duration has been reduced from 5 seconds to 3.3 seconds.
Shell-shocked: Increased buildup threshold on player ships by 20%.
Diminishing Returns

Diminishing returns have been enabled on select status effects. This is to make it more difficult to repeatedly apply these status effects that could potentially shut down your ability to retaliate in a PVP setting.
How does Diminishing Returns work?
Once a status effect is activated on a target, they gain a single stack of 45% charge resistance to that same status effect for 45 seconds.
Should the same status effect get re-activated, another stack of 45% resistance is multiplied for a total of 70% resistance to the status effect charge. This also resets the 45 second timer.
After 45 seconds without an activation one stack of resistance is removed.
Enabled diminishing returns:
Shell Shocked: Disables all your weapons for a given time and applies a one-off 3000 damage in an area.
Torn Sails: Slows your sailing speed by 75%.
Drastically reduced stamina cost of trimming while sailing by about 60% - 80% depending on the ship.

Dev Note: This change is made so that stamina management can primarily be reserved for bracing especially in PVP situations. The change is also made to reduce the need manage stamina while sailing from location to location in the Indian Ocean.
Increased accuracy of aim assist to make Boarding slightly easier.
Increased buoyant stability of the Bedar.
Dev note: This change should make aiming on the Bedar more stable and less affected by waves, and more in line with the stability of the Cutter.
Expand friction area for leading shots when aiming.
Dev note: This change should make aiming leading shots at enemies more stable and reliable.
Contextually displayed more meaningful and accurate statistics on weapon tooltips depending on the type of weapon:
Projectile Speed: Culverin, Demi-Cannon, Long Gun, Bombard, Torpedo, Ballista
Time-to-target: Mortar, Rockets
None: Sea Fire
Added Sea Lord reinforcement fleets in World Tier II upon triggering a high level of hostility.
Players will need to be in the corresponding regions for reinforcements to arrive:
Phoenix Talon – East Indies
Tides of Terror – Coast of Africa
Hubac Twins – Red Isle
Shadow Legion – Open Seas
Dev note: This was done to make it easier for players completing the Ascension Mastery contract to spawn the contract’s objectives.
Moderately increased difficulty level of each individual affix for Sea Monsters in World Tier II.
Dev note: This was done to provide a more distinct experience between fighting a Sea Monster in World Tier II compared to World Tier I.
Updated world event marker to be hidden upon entering the world event zone.
Updated world event marker to be hidden from target ship when engaging in combat.
Updated the Player Ship Rank indicator on the bottom left of the screen while at sea to turn red when in combat, indicating that Docking and Fast Travel are unavailable.

Dev note: We are aware of frustrations expressed by many of you due to hostility rules you from docking after completing an activity. We are currently treating this issue as a top priority and working on a solution that should allow players to dock after a defined amount of time spent in the safe area, despite hostility.
While this solution will be implemented in an upcoming patch, we are first implementing improvements to visual feedback to better indicate when docking is unavailable.

The Ship Rank of the Maangodin and Spectral reinforcements have been lowered.
The starting ship ranks of reinforcements will start at Ship Rank 9, lowered from starting at Ship Rank 10.

Dev note: We noted that it was difficult for players to complete Spectral Defenses alone even with Ship Rank 14 ships. We’re reducing the difficulty to make the difficulty more manageable for solo players.

Dev note: As things might get chaotic in the heat of battle, and especially in Death Tides, we’ve added additional functionality for the Voice Chat feature, which allows for gameplay audio volume to temporarily reduce while voice is being transmitted by the player or other players, through a technical feature known as “Audio Ducking”.
By enabling voice attenuation and adjusting the attenuation level, gameplay audio will “make way” for voice chat audio, making it easier to hear teammates and groupmates in battle.

Adjust this setting to select the minimum volume level needed from your microphone before it is transmitted to other players

releases.displayName: Year 2 Season 1 Patch Notes

items.text: Year 2 of Skull and Bones kicks off with a bang; the stakes are higher than ever before. Tensions rise across the Indian Ocean as Year 1 Season 4 ended with the unsettling reports that the DMC are attempting to seize the opportunity to strengthen its position in the Indian Ocean. Kicking off an arms race with the Compagnie, these two Megacorporations find themselves in a war over control of the Indian Ocean, with new technology fuelling a new age of warfare.
Weren’t able to watch our Year 2 Showcase live? Catch up on it here.
Note – Pieces of Eight will be removed from chests/caches that have been obtained prior to Y2S1 in all players’ inventory.
At Blackwood, players may choose to convert Seasonal Currency into Sovereigns at the rate of 100 Seasonal Currency (only applicable to current season’s Kupfer Bars) to 50 Sovereigns.
Silver will not be reset.

The Indian Ocean is set ablaze by the war between the Megacorporations, with each side looking to gain an advantage over the other by using increasingly powerful weapons. The origins of these ascended weapons remain a mystery, but what is known is that acquiring them may be vital to surviving the coming onslaught.

Pre-requisites: Players will need to be at least Infamy Tier 9 when a mail will be sent to the mailbox. Read the mail to start the quest “Ascension and Modification” and then make your way to the Blacksmith to unlock the Item Ascension feature.
The Blacksmiths can now Ascend your weapons, with powerful modifications.
There are three modification grades:
Basic – General improvements
Advanced – Noteworthy improvements
Special – Powerful improvements with unique properties
Modification Slots are assigned based on the weapon rarity:
Common – 2 Basic, 1 Advanced, 1 Special
Uncommon – 1 Basic, 1 Advanced, 1 Special
Rare – 2 Basic, 1 Special
Epic – 1 Basic, 1 Advanced
Equipment rarity will determine the number and grade of Ascension Slots

Using Ascension Modules, materials (Refined Materials, Specialized Material, Helm Materials, among others), Silver and Pieces of Eight, unlock modification slots for your weapons. Upon unlocking a modification slot, a random modification is automatically granted.
Ascension Modules can be obtained from:
Mythic-difficulty Chance to obtain from final stand Seasonal Sea Lord chests in World Tier 1: Shallow Waters.
Guaranteed to obtain from Final Stand Seasonal Sea Lord chest and Faction Elite Warship (i.e. Vanderkill, Rode Maangodin) in World Tier 2: Cutthroat Seas.
Purchasable from Blackwood and Yanita (limited stocks, weekly refresh).

Reforging: Using Upgrade Parts and some Silver, replace existing modifications with a random new modification. Try different combinations of modifications for your ascended weapons to fit your unique playstyle!
To unlock modification in the final slot of each equipment, an additional toolkit is required: Masterwork Kit.
Obtain Masterwork Kits from:
Successfully plundering Grand Fort and Oosten Fort in World Tier 2.
Chance to obtain from Seasonal Sea Lord Strongboxes in World Tier 2.
Chance to obtain from Ah Pak’s cargo.
Here are some examples of modifications:
Different weapon types will have different Modifications pools to reforge from.

Rockets, Demi-cannons have a lesser variant of the modification with lower proc chances to compensate. Likewise certain modifications will only be allowed on certain weapons. This list is available when you open the weapon ascension service at the blacksmith.
The sequence in which you reforge modifications will have some impact on your future modifications. This can influence your odds of getting certain modifications.
For example, reforging Incendiary on your Common Culverins will add Fire damage as a percentage of weapon damage. As a result, the weapon will henceforth be able to reforge Amplified Burning.
Care is to be taken in such a situation, if you reforge Incendiary away then Amplified Burning would remain on your weapon and the benefits would be limited.
It is possible to reforge the same modifications on the specific unique weapon.
Each weapon will have a limit on Reforge Attempts.
Each unique weapon starts off at 60 points on the Reforge Attempt. Once the Reforge attempt is used up, modifications can no longer be changed for the unique weapon.

Dev Note: Weapon Ascension is a feature created for you to push the limits of your weapons and create synergies around your build. One of our observations in Year 1 was that builds between players didn’t have the level of variance or creativity that could bring about fun. Weapons would often have a single trick, and you had to play it in a particular way.

With Weapon ascension, a simple Carronade can now serve different playstyles and help you to make your build special. At the same time, it gives you to have a wider selection of weapons when it comes to exploring builds.
Likewise, a common Culverin V could be ascended to greatness and become a supplement for you to be creative with your weaponry.

All modifications are made to be useful. But some will be highly coveted. It will take both the skill to identify what is synergistic and some luck to assemble the perfect weapons for your build, and separate good ascensions from truly great ascended weapons.

There was also the consideration of randomness. Having the power to choose specific modifications meant that everyone would have access to the great ascended weapons. We want these great ascensions to be rare – this makes the great ascensions special and something to work towards. However, a fully random system was tedious and meant bloating the item drops. To achieve this, we have opted for the combination of reforge limits and given the ability to target modifications and reforge the less desirable modifications. This is a balancing point between full randomness and choice.

We are not truly done with Ascension yet. We expect players to push this system into the unknown and find builds that might require further tuning. In our future updates, we are exploring modifications that would make build-making special, ways to trade ascended items, exploring methods for you manipulate the level of randomness and ways to extend the reforge limit, perhaps even modify modification slots – at a cost. The community feedback in this area will help us steer this forward.

notes.title: Ship Gear Score Re-Balancing, Ship Upgrades, Ship Rank, & Base Ship Rank Requirements Progression Updates

notes.title: Base Ship Rank Requirements on Items

items.text: From Year 2 Season 1, weapons, armour and furniture will have a required base ship rank.
You can only equip an item if it the targeted ship has a based ship rank is higher than that of the item’s required ship rank.
The requirement on each item will vary but will cap out at Ship Rank 4.

Note - If you had equipped an item before Year 2 Season 1, it will remain equipped and fully functional. However, if you were to un-equip that item, it cannot be re-equipped until the base ship rank requirement has been met.
Dev Note: Throughout Year 1 with the content we’ve added, we noticed there were some situations having an increasing impact:

Firstly, most of the Gear Score composition previously came from equipped Weapons and Armour. For low Ship Ranks, equipping a single armour can disproportionately increase the Ship Rank. Gear Score on auxiliary weapons was notably lower – coming from a pre-ship upgrade era where only very few ships had auxiliary slots. This has created a perception that they are less valuable, when they are just as powerful as quadrant weapons. While Ship Upgrades in Season 2 helped mitigate this, it hasn’t quite been enough.

Second, the state of the Indian Ocean today (now called World Tier 1), is tailored for players looking for entry level challenge. While it is great for onboarding, it makes most adversaries at endgame too easy once players have progressed. It has also led to players naturally skipping Ship Upgrades as these do not have the intended impact when facing higher difficulty challenges.

Third, the ability to obtain more powerful weapons, whether through trading or other players dropping equipment, means all players regardless of their progression can significantly increase their Ship Rank very quickly. This access to more powerful weapons, including Epic Weapons, as early as before the onboarding is having an impact on the pace of progression, your sense of challenge, and impact on rewards obtained as you progress.

Rewards from the Smuggler Pass and World Events are meant to have a high impact. To allow players rapid developments in their loadouts, these rewards are given out quite early in the endgame. However, equipping epic items also meant rapid Ship Rank growth very early on followed by a long progression towards Ship Rank 13.

Fourth, for most players’ their Helm Empire fleet tend to be equipped with a blend of spare items to reach the intended ship rank for the assigned Manufactory. This takes away from the experience of assembling a deadly pirate fleet. The ability to put together these builds to reach the required Ship Rank has taken away the need to upgrade ships and created a situation where these ships are rarely swapped.

These issues are relatively harmless individually but together created an environment of inconsistencies in progression, challenge and variations in skill level. Challenges amounted to increasing the number of ships at a world event and more damage output. Which consequently meant that players could quickly eliminate ships and take on onslaughts of similarly ranked content at once but then also get sunk equally fast.

With Y2S1, we have an opportunity to address some of these concerns. The adversaries of World Tier 2 will start to deal more damage and in more unique ways. As such we put emphasis on Ship Upgrades by shifting the weight of gear score toward ships and ship upgrades. This change is intended to make ship upgrades more meaningful as a gradual form of progression while also highlighting the importance of the base ship defences against the challenge of World Tier 2. For some players it will also encourage them to try different ships.

This is a big change which will have wide reaching effects on multiple areas of the game. We considered smaller changes over a longer period, but since Ship Rank is a system widely integrated into progression and endgame it means some areas feel awkward in terms of balance. Hence, we decided to make a few big changes at once instead to ensure a smoother transition.

These changes would undoubtedly impact the progression of multiple loadouts. In some cases, your Ship Rank would drop if you had not upgraded before. In other cases, your Ship Rank would go up, assuming you had upgraded but not equipped rare and epic items.
Since the case where Ship Rank drops is of greater impact. We wanted to expound on two key areas.

The first key area is where player’s Active Ship Loadout is used as the main combat ship. At this point it’s important we make something very clear: losing Ship Ranks does NOT mean a decrease in damage or defensive stats. These adjustments simply ensure that Ship Rank more accurately reflects combat potential.
The second key area is ships assigned in your Helm Empire. Most ships used in the Helm Empire have a greater proportion of being un-upgraded.
We want to share some of the steps taken to reduce the effects of this change.
The biggest one is that Ship upgrade costs have been overall lowered and more drastically for the first 3 ship upgrades.

To ease this transition, we will be compensating players with Ship Upgrade Chests, which will contain currencies and high-end materials needed to upgrade your ships. Players will receive one Upgrade Chest for each ship class, containing enough resources to upgrade one ship of that class from level 0 to level 3. Take note, this chest does not contain the materials for crafting the base ship. Combined with the reduced upgrade costs, this will help ensure that your ships are combat-ready. Note to be eligible for this, you’ll need to have played Skull and Bones anytime during Seasons 2, 3, and/or 4.

For the Helm Empire, we have adjusted the risk level of assigning ships, lower tiered Manufactories have now lower risks. High tiered manufactories will maintain their levels of risk, to reward players dedicated to upgrading their fleet.

Finally, Manufactories will be able to produce crafting materials, as covered in our Helm Empire – Year 2 Changes & Improvements DevBlog. With strategic planning, Manufactories can serve as a passive source of crafting materials to upgrade your ships.

Ship Rank is a fundamental system in Skull and Bones, we believe that by taking these steps it will create a better state of balance that should feel more consistent across the various systems as you explore the endgame challenge
Want to know more? Check out our Deep Dive into the Global Progression Rebalance.

Sainte-Anne and Telok Penjarah Job Board contracts’ objectives have been adjusted to overall reduce the amount of time required to complete each contract.

Dev Note: While aiming in Skull and Bones, the camera pitch angle is limited to a range which determines how far you can move the camera above and below the horizon.: In our explanations below, we will use a range of [-10 degrees, +10 degrees] as an illustration, but the Minimum Pitch and Maximum Pitch angles vary between weapons.

To enhance the aiming experience, we implement a concept called Camera Damping. This allows the camera parameters to gradually align with the reference point, which in this case is the camera angle. Think of it as placing the camera on a gimbal to reduce the rocky effects of the waves.: The damping effect enables the camera pitch angle to temporarily exceed its usual range, providing better comfort when aiming on rough waves, where ships tend to experience a higher degree of pitch and roll. However, this also means that the camera may deviate much more from its set pitch angle limits, causing the camera to clip into the ship.

In Y1S4.1.0, we applied a fix to reduce the damping effect to address the camera clipping into the ship. This was causing players to be unable to see their target as their view was blocked by their own ship’s mesh. By reducing the damping effect, the correction was applied faster. We inadvertently introduced a bug which made this damping reduction apply within the aiming pitch limits. It resulted in the feeling that the camera is constantly adjusted.

In Y1S4.1.3, fixed this issue by only taking into account the angle difference outside of the min/max pitch limit. This adjustment made minor deviations outside of the [-10, +10] range less affected by the damping effect, therefore reducing the negative impact of players’ ability to aim during minor deviations within the [-13, +13] range.

In this patch, we are further increasing the damping buffer range to [-19, +19]. With this change, players will not notice significant changes in aiming behaviour compared to before Y1S4.1.0 when their ship is pitched up or down by up to 9 degrees due to rough waves. This adjustment should cover a majority of cases.

We also note that this season, compared to previous ones, has more events that engage players in locations with rougher seas. This contributes to the increased feeling of aiming degradation while riding on taller waves. We are continuing to explore other options to improve the comfort of aiming in the coming patches.

We hope this detailed developer note provides deeper insight and analysis into how one of the core mechanics of our naval combat game works. Additionally, it outlines the steps we are taking to address player concerns regarding this topic.
TAUNT STATUS EFFECT
Updated Taunt Status effect to allow for faster accumulation of status effect against Elite Warships.

Dev Note: In Y1S4.1.3, we released a change to solve an issue where all AI ships had Taunted Capacity that was higher than intended. This caused a number of non-Elite ships to be killed without even triggering the status effect. To fix this, we reduced the Taunt Capacity of all AI ships. However, further analysis revealed that the Taunt Capacity of Elite ships remained high, causing the Taunt Status Effect to take a considerable amount of time to build up on Elite ships before being triggered. With this change, the Taunt Status Effect should build up approximately 3 times faster on Elite ships. This adjustment should make the status effect feel relevant in builds against Elite ships once again.

notes.title: SECONDARY DAMAGE SYSTEM CHANGES (ELEMENTAL DAMAGE CHANGES)

items.text: The Secondary Damage system for applying the various damage types has been revamped.

Previously, the amount of status effect charges applied was determined exclusively by the weapon and not by the damage type on the weapon. Going forward, this value is now tied to the secondary damage type and can now scale secondary modifiers on the weapon as well as other modifiers.
The overall experience of using weapons and fighting enemies remains and should be quite like the experience before.
Example:
Firing a projectile with 1000 base damage and 20% piercing at a target with 500 armour and 30% piercing resistance.
Armour Rating Mitigation: The 1000 base damage is reduced by 33% from armour rating to 667 damage.
Secondary Damage Resistance: 200 piercing damage is reduced by 30% piercing resistance to 140 piercing damage.
The final damage applied to the target is a total of 807 damage.
The piercing damage is then further applied as 140 charges of Punctured which is the related status effect that will be applied to the target.

releases.displayName: Update on Title Update Y1S3.1 Maintenance Issues

items.text: Greetings Captains,

We wanted to give you all an update following up on the technical issues encountered during our Title Update Y1S3.1 which was deployed during the Monday 16th September (PT) / Tuesday 17th September’s (CEST/AET) weekly maintenance.
We were forced to extend our maintenance significantly to identify and fix the source of a critical issue, causing systematic server crashes.

In addition, and thanks to the many reports and feedback received from the community, we were quickly made aware the update brought additional issues. These affected your Helm Empire and Pieces of Eight production, once our servers were made available again on Tuesday 17th September at approximately 7pm (CEST)/10am (PT)/Wednesday September 18th, 3am (AET).

An emergency maintenance was therefore triggered allowing us to address and fix those issues on Tuesday 17th September, between 7.30pm and 8pm (PT)/Wednesday September 18th, between 4.30am and 5am (CEST)/12.30pm and 1pm (AET).

As a token of appreciation for your patience and support, and to compensate for the time our game servers were unavailable, all players can expect to receive the following items through their in-game mailbox starting on Wednesday 18th September 7pm PT)/Thursday 19th September, 4am (CET)/12pm (AET).
4x Upgrade Kit
20x Greenheart Plank
20x Torsion Spring
20x Precision Drilling Bit
20x Bitterballen
20x Medium Repair Kit
20x Water Barrel
Please note that to receive the compensation you will need to log in to the game between 2am (UTC) Thursday 19th September and 2am (UTC) Tuesday 15th October.

Last but not least, we are actively investigating and monitoring the impact those issues have had on players’ progression and the amount of Pieces of Eight generated between the end of the first scheduled maintenance and the start of the emergency maintenance.

While our primary goal is to verify that reported issues are addressed, we also want to ensure that no one has unfairly benefited from those issues - and that our end-game economy remains balanced - we will do our best to avoid any progression loss made since our servers came back online.
We’ll continue to keep you regularly updated and informed of our progress on this topic, and we remain thankful for your patience and understanding.
The Skull and Bones Dev Team.

releases.displayName: Maintenance 17th September - UPDATED

items.text: UPDATE
Hello Captains,
As announced earlier today, the maintenance is being extended.

Our teams have identified a critical issue causing systematic server crashes. To ensure a smooth and stable experience for everyone, we made the decision to extend the maintenance until further notice whilst we are working on resolving the situation as quickly as possible.
We understand this is not something the community wants to hear, and this may be frustrating. We deeply appreciate your patience while our team works to fix the issue.
We'll keep you updated, and we'll let you know as soon as the servers are back online.
In the meantime, we are working on an in-game compensation plan and will give more details on this soon.
Keep an eye on our channels for further updates.
Captains,

We have identified critical issues causing server instability during the maintenance. The team are currently investigating and working to resolve the issues before reopening our servers. At this time, the game will remain in maintenance until further notice. In the meantime we deeply appreciate your patience and understanding.

Dev note: In Patch 2.2, we introduced changes to make World Events accessible on a fixed schedule. We have since been closely observing player feedback, and while the scheduling changes were generally well-received, we also noted that the community felt that the map was getting increasingly cluttered, making it difficult to locate relevant content.

In Patch 3.1, we’re making some visual tweaks to the World Event markers to reduce the space occupied, as well as making some changes to the default visibility of World Events on the map. items.text: The convoy consists of tanky drummer merchants and escort ships.

While participating in the Bounty contracts, World events and Mooncake Regatta, you may encounter these enemies:

"Defender": a heavy tank ship with high armour and high health. They deal low damage and instead contribute by manoeuvring to block your shot.

Players who have reached the Diamond Tier on the Seasonal leaderboard in Season 2 will receive the "Sovereign" ship nameplate in their inventory at the start Season 3.
A soft reset will be applied to all players who accumulated more than 300,000 Pieces of Eight.
Helm Empire upgrades will be reset.
Owned Manufactories will be reset and based on the number of manufactories that you owned at the end of Season 2; you will be rewarded with a corresponding amount of Upgrade parts
Established Territories will be reset, and based on the number of territories that you owned at the end of Season 2, you will be rewarded with a corresponding amount of Helm Leases.
SUPPLY NETWORK & ORDER REGISTRY
The Helm has caught wind of the arrival of Imperial Jade in the Indian Ocean, sparking the chase for this lucrative new Helm Ware. The Helm is paying handsomely for whoever gets their hands on them.

The "Collect All" benefit allows players to automatically collect all Pieces of Eight from every active manufactory within the territory. Collections fees cost 5% of the total sum of collected Pieces of Eight.
Specific Territorial Benefits will be carried over to and stay active in the next season, these Benefits will be indicated in the Helm Empire Management page.
"Collect All" benefit for certain territories
"Cost Reduction for Sea People by 10%" benefit.
The "Empire Administration" upgrade will overall require less Pieces of Eight to reach the highest capacity of manufactories players could own.

Multiplayer Scaling has been adjusted and will start at 2 players instead of 3. Previously we used different scaling values depending on the activity. This has been made into a single universal scaling value for consistency.
The scaled values that come from having more players are:
Hull Health
Weakpoint Health
Damage per shot (Depending on ability of the boss)
Hard ships have slightly less health and slightly more damage.
Merchant Convoys, Elite Ships, and Sea Monsters have been tuned to become easier to increase accessibility to solo players. Their overall health and damage have been reduced depending on the context.
Forts and towers remain unchanged for now with more plans coming for the future.
Old effect: "Reduces Crew Stamina Depletion by 50% while trimming in combat"
New effect: "While trimming, reduces Crew Stamina Depletion by 50% and increases armour rating by 200."

items.text: New Reward added - Rare Minor Furniture: "Langrage Barrels"
Increases Charge Rate of the Torn Sails status effect on a target by 8%.
Increases duration of the Torn Sails status effect on a target by 8%.
New item available from Rahma - Rare Minor Furniture: "Density Furnace"
Increases Charge Rate of the Flooded status effect on a target by 8%
Increases duration of the Flooded status effect on a target by 8%
New item available from Scurlock - Rare Minor Furniture: "Shell Packing Station"
Increase Area-of-effect Radius of Bombard weapons by 7%.
Reduce Reload Time of Bombard weapons by 7%.
New blueprint of existing equipment will now be available.
Its attacks now favour targets with high health.
Lowered the time it spends circling near the edge of world after phase change from 15 to 10 seconds to reduce the time it spends away from the players.
Easier to interrupt the encircle, in order to decrease the time it stays away from the player.
Increased the speed it travels underwater while repositioning to cut down the time it's not visible to the player by half.
In the last combat phase, it will reposition at normal swim height to make it easier to hit.
Last combat phase starts later to allow players to get more comfortable with the fight before the high intensity phase.
Reduced number of Ambush attacks in the last combat phase, to increase chance to deal damage to it.
In the last phase, increased the number of Bite attacks.
Decreased time it spends underwater before an Ambush attack.
Overall, the time spent underwater is reduced, making it easier to shoot.
The penalties for headwind will only apply when the ship is trimming at full sails to keep its occurrence more consistent.
The speed penalty is reduced from the 5-8 knots range down to 1-2 knots.
For the Dhow and small ships, they will experience a speed reduction of 1 knot.
For medium ships, they will experience a speed reduction of 2 knots.
The navigation widget arrow is updated. When in irons (ship has stopped), the arrow will now show an orange arrow instead of red.
The visual effects have been reduced - the player's vision is less obscured now while facing strong winds.
Players can now harvest resources by holding down the interaction button when the interact prompt appears. Using a higher tier tool will continue to grant additional resources per harvest action.
Events that are in the warm-up phase will no longer be included in the Recommendations.
Updated the onboarding flow, players will no longer play through the Atolls introduction, instead will be transported to start at Sainte-Anne after the introductory sequence.
Trade routes will evolve and change according to active World Events or Seasonal Events.
Smuggler Pass exclusive equipment can no longer be traded, sold, salvaged, jettisoned, and lost on death.

releases.displayName: An update about upcoming Free Trial

items.text: We've got an important message for you.
We want to inform you that the Free Trial for Skull and Bones will be temporarily delayed on Steam.
We understand this may be disappointing, but we’re committed to delivering the best possible experience.
We’ll keep you updated on our progress and share an update very soon.
